sentences.zh: 嘉禾

translations.literal: Excellent Grain
translations.idiomatic: Excellent Grain

sentences.zh: 嘉禾，五穀之長，王者德盛，則二苗共秀。

translations.literal: Excellent grain is the chief of the five grains; when a king's virtue is abundant, two stalks share one ear.
translations.idiomatic: Excellent grain is foremost among the five grains; when a ruler's virtue flourishes, two stalks bear a single ear.

sentences.zh: 於周德，三苗共穗；

translations.literal: Under Zhou virtue, three stalks shared one ear;
translations.idiomatic: Under the virtue of Zhou, three stalks shared one ear;

sentences.zh: 於商德，同本異穟；

translations.literal: Under Shang virtue, same root, different ears;
translations.idiomatic: Under the virtue of Shang, the roots were the same but the ears differed;

sentences.zh: 於夏德，異本同秀。

translations.literal: Under Xia virtue, different roots, same ear.
translations.idiomatic: Under the virtue of Xia, the roots differed but the ear was one.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝元康四年，嘉穀玄稷，降于郡國。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuankang of Emperor Xuan of Han, excellent grain and dark millet descended upon the commanderies and states.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuankang under Emperor Xuan of Han, excellent grain and dark millet appeared throughout the commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和中，嘉禾生郡國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, excellent grain grew in the commanderies and states.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign of Emperor Zhang of Han, excellent grain sprang up in commanderies and kingdoms across the realm.

sentences.zh: 漢安帝延光二年六月，嘉禾生九真，百五十六本，七百六十八穗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Yanguang of Emperor An of Han, excellent grain grew in Jiuzhen—one hundred fifty-six stalks and seven hundred sixty-eight ears.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Yanguang under Emperor An of Han, excellent grain appeared in Jiuzhen: one hundred fifty-six stalks bearing seven hundred sixty-eight ears.

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝建和二年四月，嘉禾生大司農帑藏。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Jianhe of Emperor Huan of Han, excellent grain grew in the treasury of the Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Jianhe under Emperor Huan of Han, excellent grain grew in the state granary overseen by the Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝永康元年八月，嘉禾生魏郡。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongkang of Emperor Huan of Han, excellent grain grew in Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongkang under Emperor Huan of Han, excellent grain appeared in Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初元年，郡國三言嘉禾生。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangchu of Emperor Wen of Wei, three commanderies and states reported that excellent grain had grown.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, three commanderies and kingdoms reported the growth of excellent grain.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權黃龍三年十月，會稽南始平言嘉禾生。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Huanglong of Sun Quan of Wu, Nan Shiping in Kuaiji reported that excellent grain had grown.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year of Huanglong under Sun Quan of Wu, Nan Shiping in Kuaiji reported that excellent grain had appeared.

sentences.zh: 孫權赤烏七年秋，宛陵言嘉禾生。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year of Chiwu of Sun Quan, Wanling reported that excellent grain had grown.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year of Chiwu under Sun Quan, Wanling reported the growth of excellent grain.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始八年十月，瀘水胡王彭護獻嘉禾。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, Peng Hu, king of the Lushui Hu, presented excellent grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eighth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, Peng Hu, king of the Lushui Hu, presented excellent grain as tribute.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康四年十二月，嘉禾生扶風雍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, excellent grain grew in Fufeng and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, excellent grain appeared in Fufeng and Yong.

sentences.zh: 太康五年七月，嘉禾生豫章南昌。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Taikang, excellent grain grew in Yuzhang and Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Taikang, excellent grain grew in Yuzhang and Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 太康八年閏三月，嘉禾生東夷校尉園。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month of the eighth year of Taikang, excellent grain grew in the garden of the Commandant of the Eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month of the eighth year of Taikang, excellent grain appeared in the garden of the Commandant of the Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 太康八年九月，嘉禾生東萊掖。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Taikang, excellent grain grew in Donglai and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Taikang, excellent grain grew in Donglai and Ye.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建興元年八月癸亥，嘉禾生襄平縣，一莖七穗。

translations.literal: On the guihai day of the eighth month of the first year of Jianxing of Emperor Min of Jin, excellent grain grew in Xiangping County—one stalk with seven ears.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day of the eighth month of the first year of Jianxing under Emperor Min of Jin, excellent grain appeared in Xiangping County, a single stalk bearing seven ears.

sentences.zh: 建興二年六月，嘉禾生平州治，三實同蔕。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Jianxing, excellent grain grew at the seat of Ping Province—three fruits sharing one stem.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Jianxing, excellent grain grew at the provincial capital of Pingzhou, three grains on one stem.

sentences.zh: 建興三年七月，嘉禾生襄平縣，異體同蔕。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Jianxing, excellent grain grew in Xiangping County—different bodies sharing one stem.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year of Jianxing, excellent grain appeared in Xiangping County, separate stalks joined by a single stem.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二年十月，嘉禾生潁川陽翟，太守垣苗以聞。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, excellent grain grew in Yangzhai, Yingchuan; the grand administrator Yuan Miao reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, excellent grain appeared in Yangzhai in Yingchuan, and Grand Administrator Yuan Miao notified the court.

sentences.zh: 元嘉九年三月，嘉禾生義陽，豫州刺史長沙王義欣以獻。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Yiyang; the Inspector of Yuzhou, the Prince of Changsha Yixing, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Yiyang, and Yixing, Prince of Changsha and Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十年八月，嘉禾生汝南苞信，豫州刺史長沙王義欣以獻。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the tenth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Baoxin, Runan; the Inspector of Yuzhou, the Prince of Changsha Yixing, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the tenth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in Baoxin in Runan, and Yixing, Prince of Changsha and Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十一年八月，嘉禾一莖九穗生北汝陰，太守王玄謨以獻。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eleventh year of Yuanjia, excellent grain with one stalk and nine ears grew in North Ruyin; the grand administrator Wang Xuanmo presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eleventh year of Yuanjia, a stalk of excellent grain bearing nine ears grew in North Ruyin, and Grand Administrator Wang Xuanmo presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年六月，嘉禾一莖九穗生上庸新安，梁州刺史劉真道以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain with one stalk and nine ears grew in Shangyong and Xin'an; the Inspector of Liangzhou Liu Zhendao presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain with one stalk and nine ears appeared in Shangyong and Xin'an, and Liu Zhendao, Inspector of Liangzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十一年，嘉禾生新野鄧縣，雍州刺史蕭思話以獻。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Deng County, Xinye; the Inspector of Yongzhou Xiao Sihua presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Deng County in Xinye, and Xiao Sihua, Inspector of Yongzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年六月，嘉禾生籍田，一莖九穗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in the sacred plow fields—one stalk with nine ears.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in the sacred plow fields, a single stalk bearing nine ears.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年七月癸酉，嘉禾生平虜陵，徐州刺史臧質以獻。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day of the seventh month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Pingluling; the Inspector of Xuzhou Zang Zhi presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the seventh month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Pingluling, and Zang Zhi, Inspector of Xuzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年九月，嘉禾生太尉府田，太尉江夏王義恭以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in the fields of the Grand Commandant's office; the Grand Commandant, the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in the fields attached to the Grand Commandant's office, and Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia and Grand Commandant, notified the court.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年九月，嘉禾生揚州東耕田，刺史始興王濬以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in the eastern plow fields of Yangzhou; the Inspector, the Prince of Shixing Jun, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in the eastern plow fields of Yangzhou, and Jun, Prince of Shixing and provincial inspector, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年，嘉禾生華林園，百六十穗，園丞陳襲祖以聞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in the Hualin Park—one hundred sixty ears; the park director Chen Xizu reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in Hualin Park with one hundred sixty ears, and Park Director Chen Xizu notified the court.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年，嘉禾生潁川曲陽，豫州刺史趙伯符以獻。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Quyang, Yingchuan; the Inspector of Yuzhou Zhao Bofu presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Quyang in Yingchuan, and Zhao Bofu, Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十三年七月乙丑，嘉禾旅生籍田，籍田令褚熙伯以聞。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in clusters in the sacred plow fields; the director of the plow fields Chu Xibo reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain sprang up in clusters in the sacred plow fields, and Chu Xibo, director of those fields, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十三年七月庚午，嘉禾生丹陽椒唐里，揚州刺史始興王濬以聞。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day of the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Jiaotang Lane, Danyang; the Inspector of Yangzhou, the Prince of Shixing Jun, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in Jiaotang Lane in Danyang, and Jun, Prince of Shixing and Inspector of Yangzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十三年七月庚辰，嘉禾生醴湖屯，屯主王世宗以聞。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day of the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew at the Lihu garrison; the garrison chief Wang Shizong reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day of the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew at the Lihu garrison, and Garrison Chief Wang Shizong notified the court.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十三年八月己酉，嘉禾生華林園，園丞陳襲祖以聞。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day of the eighth month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Hualin Park; the park director Chen Xizu reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the eighth month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in Hualin Park, and Park Director Chen Xizu reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十三年九月庚申，嘉禾生沛郡蕭，征北大將軍衡陽王義季以聞。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day of the ninth month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Xiao, Pei Commandery; the General Who Conquers the North, the Prince of Hengyang Yiji, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the ninth month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Xiao in Pei Commandery, and Yiji, Prince of Hengyang and General Who Conquers the North, notified the court.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十三年，嘉禾生江夏汝南，荊州刺史南譙王義宣以聞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Jiangxia and Runan; the Inspector of Jingzhou, the Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in Jiangxia and Runan, and Yixuan, Prince of Nanqiao and Inspector of Jingzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十四年七月乙卯，嘉禾旅生華林園及景陽山，園丞梅道念以聞。

translations.literal: On the yimao day of the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in clusters in Hualin Park and on Jingyang Hill; the park director Mei Daonian reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day of the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain sprang up in clusters in Hualin Park and on Jingyang Hill, and Park Director Mei Daonian notified the court.

sentences.zh: 太尉江夏王義恭上表曰：

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant, the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant, Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: :臣聞居高聽卑，上帝之功；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that to dwell on high and listen below is the work of the Supreme Lord;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that to dwell on high and heed what lies below is the work of the Supreme Lord;

sentences.zh: 天且弗違，聖王之德。

translations.literal: what Heaven does not oppose is the virtue of a sage king.
translations.idiomatic: and what Heaven does not oppose is the virtue of a sage king.

sentences.zh: 故能影響二儀，甄陶萬有。

translations.literal: Thus one can influence the Two Principles and shape the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: By such virtue one may sway the two cosmic forces and shape the myriad things of creation.

sentences.zh: 鑒觀今古，採驗圖緯，未有道闕化虧，而禎物著明者也。

translations.literal: Surveying past and present and testing charts and weft-texts, there has never been a time when the Way was lacking and transformation failed, yet auspicious things shone forth clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying past and present and testing the charts and weft-texts, never has the Way been wanting and transformation been impaired while auspicious things still shone forth in plain sight.

sentences.zh: 自皇運受終，辰曜交和，是以卉木表靈，山淵効寶。

translations.literal: Since the imperial mandate was received at the end of the cycle, the stellar radiances have mingled in harmony; hence plants and trees display numinous signs, and mountains and streams yield their treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial mandate passed into your house and the stars have moved in harmony, plants and trees have shown their numinous power and mountains and streams have offered up their treasures.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下體乾統極，休符襲逮。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty embodies Qian and governs the ultimate pole; blessed tokens have come in succession.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty embodies the power of Qian and holds the supreme pole of rule, while blessed tokens have arrived one after another.

sentences.zh: 若乃鳳儀西郊，龍見東邑，海酋獻改緇之羽，河祇開俟清之源。

translations.literal: As for the phoenix displaying its bearing in the western suburbs, the dragon appearing in the eastern city, sea chieftains presenting feathers changed from black, and the river god opening the source that awaits purification—
translations.idiomatic: Whether it is the phoenix showing its bearing in the western suburbs, the dragon appearing in the eastern capital, sea lords presenting feathers turned from black, or the river god revealing the source that waits to be made clear—

sentences.zh: 三代象德，不能過也。

translations.literal: the symbolic virtue of the Three Dynasties could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: not even the symbolic virtue of the Three Dynasties could surpass this.

sentences.zh: 有幽必闡，無遠弗屆，重譯歲至，休瑞月臻。

translations.literal: What is hidden must be disclosed; nothing remote lies beyond reach; interpreters through many translations come year by year, and auspicious omens arrive month by month.
translations.idiomatic: What lies hidden is surely brought to light; nothing remote lies beyond your reach; envoys through many tongues come year after year, and blessed omens arrive month by month.

sentences.zh: 前者躬籍南畝，嘉穀仍植，神明之應，在斯尤盛。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Your Majesty personally plowed the southern fields, excellent grain was planted again—the response of the spirits is nowhere more abundant.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty lately plowed the southern fields in person, excellent grain grew there again; the response of the spirits is nowhere more abundant than in this.

sentences.zh: 四海既穆，五民樂業，思述汾陽，經始靈囿。

translations.literal: The four seas are already tranquil, the five peoples rejoice in their occupations; you thought to follow the example of Fenyang and began the numinous park.
translations.idiomatic: The four seas are at peace, the five peoples rejoice in their work, and you turned your thoughts to the example of Fenyang and began the numinous park.

sentences.zh: 蘭林甫樹，嘉露頻流，板築初就，祥穟如積。

translations.literal: The Orchid Grove had just been planted when fine dew flowed again and again; the rammed-earth works were newly completed, and auspicious grain heaped up like a mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Orchid Grove had scarcely been planted when sweet dew flowed again and again; the rammed-earth works were barely finished when auspicious grain heaped up like a mound.

sentences.zh: 太平之符，於是乎在。

translations.literal: The tokens of great peace are here.
translations.idiomatic: The signs of great peace are manifest here.

sentences.zh: 臣以寡立，承乏槐鉉，沐浴芳津，預覩冥慶，不勝抃儛之情。

translations.literal: Your subject, established in few accomplishments, has undertaken the weary burden of the locust-tree mace; bathed in fragrant blessings, I have witnessed these hidden felicitations and cannot contain my joy of clapping and dancing.
translations.idiomatic: I, established in few accomplishments, have taken on the weary burden of the Grand Commandant's staff; bathed in your fragrant grace, I have witnessed these hidden blessings and cannot contain my joy.

sentences.zh: 謹上嘉禾甘露頌一篇，不足稱揚美烈，追用悚汗。

translations.literal: I respectfully submit one hymn in praise of excellent grain and sweet dew, insufficient to proclaim your splendid virtue, and follow it with fearful sweat.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit one hymn in praise of excellent grain and sweet dew, though it is insufficient to proclaim your splendid virtue, and I do so with fearful reverence.

sentences.zh: 其頌曰：

translations.literal: The hymn reads:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

sentences.zh: :二象攸分，三靈樂主。

translations.literal: The two images were then divided; the three numina rejoiced in their lord.
translations.idiomatic: The two cosmic images were divided, and the three numina rejoiced in their lord.

sentences.zh: 齊應合從，在今猶古。

translations.literal: Qi responded and joined in accord; today is still like antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's responses joined in accord; today is still as in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 天道誰親，唯仁斯輔。

translations.literal: Whom does the Way of Heaven favor? Only the humane does it aid.
translations.idiomatic: Whom does Heaven favor? Only the humane does it sustain.

sentences.zh: 皇功帝績，理冠區宇。

translations.literal: Imperial achievements and dynastic deeds—their principle crowns the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial achievements and dynastic deeds rise above all within the realm.

sentences.zh: 四民均極，我后體茲。

translations.literal: The four peoples reach their utmost; our sovereign embodies this.
translations.idiomatic: The four peoples reach their fulfillment, and our sovereign embodies this.

sentences.zh: 惟機惟神，敬昭文思。

translations.literal: Solely perceptive, solely numinous—reverently displaying cultured thought.
translations.idiomatic: Perceptive and numinous, reverently displaying cultured thought.

sentences.zh: 九族既睦，萬邦允釐。

translations.literal: The nine kindreds are already harmonious; the ten thousand states are truly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: The nine kindreds are at peace, and the myriad states are truly well governed.

sentences.zh: 德以位敍，道致雍熙。

translations.literal: Virtue is arrayed by rank; the Way brings harmonious splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue is arrayed by rank, and the Way brings harmonious splendor.

sentences.zh: 於穆不已，顯允東儲。

translations.literal: Solemn and unceasing, the illustrious and faithful Eastern Heir.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn and unceasing is the illustrious and faithful heir apparent in the east.

sentences.zh: 生知夙叡，嶽茂淵虛。

translations.literal: Born knowing, sagely perceptive from of old; like a peak in luxuriance, like an abyss in emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing from birth, sagely wise from of old; lofty as a peak, deep as an abyss.

sentences.zh: 因心則哲，令問弘敷。

translations.literal: Following the heart, one becomes wise; fine renown spreads broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Following the heart makes one wise, and his fine renown spreads far and wide.

sentences.zh: 繼徽下武，儷景辰居。

translations.literal: Continuing the emblem below Wu, matching the splendor of the dwelling of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He continues the emblem of King Wu below, matching the splendor of the celestial dwelling.

sentences.zh: 軒制合宮，漢興未央。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor established the Hall of Union; Han rose with Everlasting Joy.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor built the Hall of Union; Han rose with the Palace of Everlasting Joy.

sentences.zh: 矧伊聖朝，九有已康。

translations.literal: How much more so this sacred court—the nine realms are already at peace.
translations.idiomatic: How much more so in this sacred court, where the nine realms are already at peace.

sentences.zh: 率由舊典，思燭前王。

translations.literal: Following the old statutes, thought illuminates the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Following the old statutes, your thought illuminates the ways of former kings.

sentences.zh: 乃造陵霄，遂作景陽。

translations.literal: Then you built Lingxiao and went on to make Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Then you raised Lingxiao and went on to build Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 有藹景陽，天淵之涘。

translations.literal: Jingyang stands luxuriant on the shore between Heaven and the abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Luxuriant stands Jingyang on the border between Heaven and the deep.

sentences.zh: 清暑爽立，雲堂特起。

translations.literal: The Clear-Summer Hall rises refreshingly; the Cloud Hall rises exceptionally.
translations.idiomatic: The Clear-Summer Hall rises cool and bright; the Cloud Hall towers apart.

sentences.zh: 植類斯育，動類斯止。

translations.literal: Planted kinds are thus nurtured; moving kinds are thus stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Planted things are nurtured here, and living things find rest.

sentences.zh: 極望江波，遍對岳峙。

translations.literal: Gazing to the limit at the river's waves, facing everywhere the peaks that stand like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: One gazes to the limit upon the river's waves and faces on every side peaks that stand like mountains.

sentences.zh: 化德惟達，休瑞惟懋。

translations.literal: Transforming virtue alone reaches far; blessed omens alone flourish abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: Transforming virtue alone extends far, and blessed omens alone flourish abundantly.

sentences.zh: 誕降嘉種，呈祥初構。

translations.literal: Excellent seed is sent down; auspicious signs appear at the first construction.
translations.idiomatic: Excellent seed descends from above, and auspicious signs appear at the first building.

sentences.zh: 甘露春凝，禎穟秋秀。

translations.literal: Sweet dew congeals in spring; auspicious grain ripens in autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet dew gathers in spring, and auspicious grain ripens in autumn.

sentences.zh: 含滋匪烈，嗣歲仍富。

translations.literal: Containing moisture, not harsh; succeeding years remain abundant.
translations.idiomatic: It holds moisture without harshness, and the years that follow remain rich.

sentences.zh: 昔在放勳，曆莢數朝。

translations.literal: Long ago under Emperor Yao, the calendar-pod appeared through several reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago under Emperor Yao, the calendar-pod appeared through several reigns.

sentences.zh: 降及重華，倚扇清庖。

translations.literal: Descending to Emperor Shun, leaning on the fan in the clear kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: It came down to Emperor Shun, who leaned on his fan in the clear kitchen.

sentences.zh: 鑠矣皇慶，比物競昭。

translations.literal: Brilliant is the imperial felicity; comparing things, each vies to shine forth.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant is the imperial felicity; among such things, each vies to shine forth.

sentences.zh: 倫彼典策，被此風謠。

translations.literal: Matching those canonical records, spreading these wind-songs.
translations.idiomatic: It matches those records in the classics and spreads these songs on the wind.

sentences.zh: 資臣六蔽，任兼兩司。

translations.literal: Your subject suffers the six obscurations and bears duties in two offices.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject suffers the six obscurations and bears duties in two offices.

sentences.zh: 既恧仲袞，又慚鄭緇。

translations.literal: I am already ashamed before Zhong Kui and also abashed before Zheng Zi.
translations.idiomatic: I am ashamed before Zhong Kui and abashed before Zheng Zi as well.

sentences.zh: 豈忘衡泌，樂道明時。

translations.literal: How could I forget Heng and Bi? I rejoice in the Way in this enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: How could I forget the reclusion of Heng and Bi? I rejoice in the Way in this enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 敢述休祉，愧闕令辭。

translations.literal: I dare to recount these blessed felicitations, ashamed that fine words are lacking.
translations.idiomatic: I dare recount these blessed felicitations, ashamed that fine words fail me.

sentences.zh: 中領軍吉陽縣侯沈演之奏上嘉禾頌曰：「煥炳禎圖，昭晰瑞典。

translations.literal: The Central Palace Guard General, Marquis of Jiyang Xian Shen Yanzhi submitted a hymn in praise of excellent grain, saying: "Radiant and brilliant is the auspicious chart; clear and bright is the blessed omen.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yanzhi, Central Palace Guard General and Marquis of Jiyang County, submitted a hymn in praise of excellent grain that read: "Radiant and brilliant is the auspicious chart; clear and bright is the blessed omen.

sentences.zh: 運傾方閟，時亨始顯。

translations.literal: The cycle tilts and the square is closed; the season of prosperity first appears.
translations.idiomatic: The cycle turns and the gate is shut; the season of prosperity first appears.

sentences.zh: 綈狀既章，鳥文斯辨。

translations.literal: The brocade pattern is already displayed; bird script is then distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The brocade pattern is already displayed, and bird script is then made plain.

sentences.zh: 於皇聖辟，承物紀遠。

translations.literal: Oh, the august sacred sovereign—receiving things, recording what is remote.
translations.idiomatic: Oh, the august sacred sovereign, who receives all things and records what lies far off.

sentences.zh: 明兩辰麗，昌輝天衍。

translations.literal: The two bright ones adorn the stars; flourishing splendor extends through Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The two bright ones adorn the stars, and flourishing splendor spreads through Heaven.

sentences.zh: 〈其一〉

translations.literal: 〈One〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈One〉

sentences.zh: 理妙位崇，事神業盛。

translations.literal: Principle is subtle, position is lofty; serving the spirits, achievement flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: His principle is subtle and his position exalted; serving the spirits, his achievement flourishes.

sentences.zh: 淵渥德澤，虛寂道政。

translations.literal: Deep and rich is his virtuous grace; empty and still is his governance by the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and rich is his virtuous grace; empty and still is his governance by the Way.

sentences.zh: 協化安心，調樂移性。

translations.literal: Harmonizing transformation, settling hearts; adjusting music, shifting natures.
translations.idiomatic: He harmonizes transformation and settles hearts; he adjusts music and shifts natures.

sentences.zh: 玉衡從體，瑤光得正。

translations.literal: The Jade Balance follows the body; the Luminous Radiance obtains rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Balance follows his person, and the Luminous Radiance holds true alignment.

sentences.zh: 巨星垂采，景雲立慶。

translations.literal: The great star lowers its brilliance; the auspicious cloud establishes felicity.
translations.idiomatic: The great star lowers its radiance, and the auspicious cloud establishes celebration.

sentences.zh: 〈其二〉

translations.literal: 〈Two〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Two〉

sentences.zh: 極仁所被，罔幽不攘。

translations.literal: Where utmost benevolence spreads, no hidden place is left unrestored.
translations.idiomatic: Where utmost benevolence reaches, no hidden corner is left unrestored.

sentences.zh: 至和所感，靡況弗彰。

translations.literal: What utmost harmony touches—no condition fails to shine forth.
translations.idiomatic: What utmost harmony touches, no condition fails to shine forth.

sentences.zh: 鴛出丹穴，鸚起西湘。

translations.literal: The yuan-bird emerges from the cinnabar cave; the parrot rises in western Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The yuan-bird emerges from the cinnabar cave, and the parrot rises in western Xiang.

sentences.zh: 白鹿踰海，素鳥越江。

translations.literal: The white deer crosses the sea; the plain bird crosses the river.
translations.idiomatic: The white deer crosses the sea, and the plain bird crosses the river.

sentences.zh: 結響穹陰，儀形鍾陽。

translations.literal: Sound knots in the vault of yin; form is patterned in the bell of yang.
translations.idiomatic: Sound gathers in the vault of yin, and form is patterned in the bell of yang.

sentences.zh: 〈其三〉

translations.literal: 〈Three〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Three〉

sentences.zh: 治人奉天，迺勤迺格。

translations.literal: Governing the people and serving Heaven—thus diligent, thus attaining.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the people and serving Heaven, he is diligent and attains his aim.

sentences.zh: 黛耒俶載，高廩已積。

translations.literal: Black plow and starting carriage—the high granaries are already filled.
translations.idiomatic: With black plow and starting carriage, the high granaries are already filled.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾重穋，甘露流液。

translations.literal: Excellent grain with double ears; sweet dew flows in liquid.
translations.idiomatic: Excellent grain bears double ears, and sweet dew flows in streams.

sentences.zh: 擢秀辰畦，揚穎角澤。

translations.literal: Raising splendor in the morning plots, displaying grain at the corner of the marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Splendor rises in the morning plots, and grain displays itself at the corner of the marsh.

sentences.zh: 離穟合豪，榮區蔭斥。

translations.literal: Separate ears joined in awn; glory spreads shade across the expanse.
translations.idiomatic: Separate ears join in one awn, and glory spreads shade across the expanse.

sentences.zh: 〈其四〉

translations.literal: 〈Four〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Four〉

sentences.zh: 盈箱徵殷，貫桑表周。

translations.literal: Filling boxes marks Yin; threading mulberry marks Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Filling boxes marks the age of Yin, and threading mulberry marks the age of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 今我大宋，靈貺綢繆。

translations.literal: Now in our great Song, numinous gifts are abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Now in our great Song, numinous gifts abound without end.

sentences.zh: 帝終撝謙，繹思勿休。

translations.literal: The Emperor to the end holds back and is modest; he unravels thought without rest.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor to the end holds back and is modest, unraveling thought without rest.

sentences.zh: 躬薦宗廟，溫恭率由。

translations.literal: In person he offers to the ancestral temples, warm and reverent, following the way.
translations.idiomatic: In person he offers to the ancestral temples, warm and reverent, following the established way.

sentences.zh: 降福以誠，孝享虔羞。

translations.literal: Blessings descend through sincerity; filial offerings are reverent sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings descend through sincerity, and filial offerings are reverent sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 〈其五〉

translations.literal: 〈Five〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Five〉

sentences.zh: 頒趾推功，登徽叡詔。

translations.literal: Extending merit to the foot, promoting achievement; ascending to brilliant sagely edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He extends merit to the lowest ranks and promotes achievement, ascending to brilliant sagely edicts.

sentences.zh: 恩覃隱顯，賞延荒徼。

translations.literal: Grace reaches hidden and manifest; rewards extend to remote frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: His grace reaches hidden and manifest alike, and rewards extend to the remotest frontiers.

sentences.zh: 河溓海夷，山華岳燿。

translations.literal: The rivers are clear, the seas are level; mountains flower, peaks blaze.
translations.idiomatic: The rivers are clear and the seas are calm; mountains flower and peaks blaze with splendor.

sentences.zh: 憬琛敻賮，兼澤委效。

translations.literal: Distant tribes bring tribute from afar; combined grace is entrusted in service.
translations.idiomatic: Distant tribes bring tribute from afar, and combined grace is entrusted in loyal service.

sentences.zh: 日表地外，改服請教。

translations.literal: The sun marks lands beyond; they change their dress and request instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Lands beyond the sun's reach change their dress and request instruction.

sentences.zh: 〈其六〉

translations.literal: 〈Six〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Six〉

sentences.zh: 茂對盛時，綏萬屢豐。

translations.literal: Abundant response to a flourishing age; pacifying the myriad, again and again abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Abundant response to a flourishing age; he pacifies the myriad realms, again and again in plenty.

sentences.zh: 厭厭歸素，秩秩大同。

translations.literal: Peacefully returning to simplicity; orderly great unity.
translations.idiomatic: Peacefully returning to simplicity, orderly great unity prevails.

sentences.zh: 上藏諸用，下知所從。

translations.literal: Above, storing it in function; below, knowing what to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Above, he stores it in function; below, all know what to follow.

sentences.zh: 仰式王度，俯歌南風。

translations.literal: Looking up to model the king's measure; bending down to sing the southern winds.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up, he models the king's measure; bending down, he sings the southern winds.

sentences.zh: 鴻名稱首，永保無窮。」

translations.literal: A great name is proclaimed foremost, preserved forever without end."
translations.idiomatic: A great name is proclaimed foremost, to be preserved forever without end."

sentences.zh: 〈其七〉

translations.literal: 〈Seven〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Seven〉

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十四年八月乙巳，嘉禾生魚城內晉陵，南徐州刺史廣陵王誕以聞。

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Jingling within Yucheng; the Inspector of South Xuzhou, the Prince of Guangling Dan, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in Jingling within Yucheng, and Dan, Prince of Guangling and Inspector of South Xuzhou, notified the court.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年六月壬寅，嘉禾旅生華林園，十株七百穗，園丞梅道念以聞。

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in clusters in Hualin Park—ten stalks and seven hundred ears; the park director Mei Daonian reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day of the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain sprang up in clusters in Hualin Park, ten stalks bearing seven hundred ears, and Park Director Mei Daonian reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年六月壬子，嘉禾生籍田，籍田令褚熙伯以獻。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in the sacred plow fields; the director of the plow fields Chu Xibo presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in the sacred plow fields, and Chu Xibo, director of those fields, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年七月壬辰，嘉禾生北海，青、冀二州刺史杜坦以獻。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Beihai; the Inspectors of Qing and Ji, Du Tan, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in Beihai, and Du Tan, Inspector of Qing and Ji, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年八月丙午，嘉禾生太尉江夏王義恭果園，江夏國典書令陳穎以聞。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day of the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in the orchard of the Grand Commandant, the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong; the Director of Documents of Jiangxia State Chen Ying reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day of the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in the orchard of Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia and Grand Commandant, and Chen Ying, Director of Documents of Jiangxia State, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年八月壬子，嘉禾生建康化義里，令丘珍孫以獻。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Huayili, Jiankang; the magistrate Qiu Zhensun presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in Huayili in Jiankang, and Magistrate Qiu Zhensun presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年八月癸丑，嘉禾生華林園，園丞梅道念以獻。

translations.literal: On the guichou day of the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Hualin Park; the park director Mei Daonian presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day of the eighth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Hualin Park, and Park Director Mei Daonian presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年十一月，嘉禾生巴東，荊州刺史南譙王義宣以聞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Badong; the Inspector of Jingzhou, the Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in Badong, and Yixuan, Prince of Nanqiao and Inspector of Jingzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年五月癸酉，嘉禾生建康禁中里，揚州刺史始興王濬以獻。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day of the fifth month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Jinzhongli, Jiankang; the Inspector of Yangzhou, the Prince of Shixing Jun, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the fifth month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Jinzhongli in Jiankang, and Jun, Prince of Shixing and Inspector of Yangzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年六月甲寅，嘉禾生籍田，籍田令褚熙伯以獻。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day of the sixth month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in the sacred plow fields; the director of the plow fields Chu Xibo presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the sixth month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in the sacred plow fields, and Chu Xibo presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年七月，嘉禾生巴東朐䏰，荊州刺史南譙王義宣以獻。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Quyang, Badong; the Inspector of Jingzhou, the Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared in Quyang in Badong, and Yixuan, Prince of Nanqiao and Inspector of Jingzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年十月己丑，嘉禾生北海，青州刺史杜坦以聞。

translations.literal: On the jichou day of the tenth month of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Beihai; the Inspector of Qingzhou Du Tan reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day of the tenth month of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew in Beihai, and Du Tan, Inspector of Qingzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十八年七月戊戌，嘉禾生廣陵邵伯埭，兗州刺史江夏王義恭以聞。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day of the seventh month of the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain grew at Shaobo Dam in Guangling; the Inspector of Yanzhou, the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the seventh month of the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia, excellent grain appeared at Shaobo Dam in Guangling, and Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia and Inspector of Yanzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝孝建二年六月癸巳，嘉禾二株生江夏王義恭東田。

translations.literal: On the guisi day of the sixth month of the second year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiao of Song, two stalks of excellent grain grew in the eastern fields of the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day of the sixth month of the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiao of Song, two stalks of excellent grain grew in the eastern fields of Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年九月己丑朔，嘉禾異畝同穎生齊郡廣饒縣。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, jichou, of the second year of Xiaojian, excellent grain with different furrows but the same ear grew in Guangrao County, Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month of the second year of Xiaojian, excellent grain with different furrows but the same ear appeared in Guangrao County in Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年七月庚午，嘉禾生吳興武康。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day of the seventh month of the third year of Xiaojian, excellent grain grew in Wukang, Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the seventh month of the third year of Xiaojian, excellent grain appeared in Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明元年五月戊午，嘉禾一株五莖生清暑殿鴟尾中。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day of the fifth month of the first year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, one stalk of excellent grain with five stems grew within the owl-tail ornament of the Clear-Summer Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the fifth month of the first year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, a single stalk of excellent grain with five stems grew within the owl-tail ornament of the Clear-Summer Hall.

sentences.zh: 大明元年八月甲申，嘉禾生青州，異根同穗。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day of the eighth month of the first year of Daming, excellent grain grew in Qing Province—different roots, same ear.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the eighth month of the first year of Daming, excellent grain appeared in Qing Province, separate roots joined by a single ear.

sentences.zh: 大明三年九月乙亥，嘉禾生北海都昌縣，青州刺史顏師伯以聞。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the ninth month of the third year of Daming, excellent grain grew in Duchang County, Beihai; the Inspector of Qingzhou Yan Shibo reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the ninth month of the third year of Daming, excellent grain grew in Duchang County in Beihai, and Yan Shibo, Inspector of Qingzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 大明六年八月辛未，嘉禾生樂陵，青、冀二州刺史劉道隆以聞。

translations.literal: On the xinwei day of the eighth month of the sixth year of Daming, excellent grain grew in Leling; the Inspectors of Qing and Ji, Liu Daolong, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the eighth month of the sixth year of Daming, excellent grain appeared in Leling, and Liu Daolong, Inspector of Qing and Ji, reported it.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始二年七月己酉，嘉禾生會稽永興，太守巴陵王休若以獻。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day of the seventh month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, excellent grain grew in Yongxing, Kuaiji; the grand administrator, the Prince of Baling Xiuyi, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the seventh month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, excellent grain grew in Yongxing in Kuaiji, and Xiuyi, Prince of Baling and grand administrator, presented it.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和中，嘉麥生郡國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, excellent wheat grew in the commanderies and states.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign of Emperor Zhang of Han, excellent wheat appeared in commanderies and kingdoms across the realm.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康十年六月，嘉麥生扶風郡，一莖四穗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, excellent wheat grew in Fufeng Commandery—one stalk with four ears.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the tenth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, excellent wheat appeared in Fufeng Commandery, a single stalk bearing four ears.

sentences.zh: 是歲收三倍。

translations.literal: That year the harvest was threefold.
translations.idiomatic: That year the harvest was three times the usual yield.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十三年，醴湖屯生嘉粟，一莖九穗，屯主王世宗以聞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, excellent millet grew at the Lihu garrison—one stalk with nine ears; the garrison chief Wang Shizong reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, excellent millet grew at the Lihu garrison, one stalk bearing nine ears, and Garrison Chief Wang Shizong reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年六月壬子，嘉黍生籍田，籍田令褚熙伯以獻。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent glutinous millet grew in the sacred plow fields; the director of the plow fields Chu Xibo presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, excellent glutinous millet grew in the sacred plow fields, and Chu Xibo presented it.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權黃龍三年，由拳野稻生，改由拳為禾興。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huanglong of Sun Quan of Wu, wild rice grew in Youquan; Youquan was renamed Hexing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huanglong under Sun Quan of Wu, wild rice appeared in Youquan, and the place was renamed Hexing.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮五鳳元年，交阯稗草化為稻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wufeng of Sun Liang of Wu, barnyard grass in Jiaozhi transformed into rice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wufeng under Sun Liang of Wu, barnyard grass in Jiaozhi transformed into rice.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十三年，吳郡嘉興鹽官縣野稻自生三十許種，揚州刺史始興王濬以聞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, wild rice grew by itself in Yanguan County, Jiaxing, Wu Commandery—some thirty kinds; the Inspector of Yangzhou, the Prince of Shixing Jun, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, wild rice sprang up by itself in Yanguan County in Jiaxing, Wu Commandery, in some thirty varieties, and Jun, Prince of Shixing and Inspector of Yangzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十八年七月癸卯，尋陽柴桑菽粟旅生，彌漫原野，江州刺史建平王宏以聞。

translations.literal: On the guimao day of the seventh month of the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia, beans and millet grew in clusters in Chaisang, Xunyang, spreading across the open fields; the Inspector of Jiangzhou, the Prince of Jianping Hong, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day of the seventh month of the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia, beans and millet sprang up in clusters in Chaisang in Xunyang and spread across the open fields, and Hong, Prince of Jianping and Inspector of Jiangzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和中，嘉瓜生郡國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, excellent melons grew in the commanderies and states.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign of Emperor Zhang of Han, excellent melons appeared in commanderies and kingdoms across the realm.

sentences.zh: 漢安帝元初三年三月，東平陵有瓜異處共生，八瓜同蔕。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Yuanchu of Emperor An of Han, in Dongpingling melons grew together at an unusual spot—eight melons sharing one stem.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Yuanchu under Emperor An of Han, in Dongpingling melons grew together at an unusual spot, eight melons on one stem.

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝建和二年七月，河東有嘉瓜，兩體共蔕。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Jianhe of Emperor Huan of Han, in Hedong there was an excellent melon—two bodies sharing one stem.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Jianhe under Emperor Huan of Han, an excellent melon appeared in Hedong, two fruits on one stem.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康三年六月，嘉瓜異體同蔕，生河南洛陽輔國大將軍王濬園。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, an excellent melon with different bodies sharing one stem grew in the garden of the Supporting-State General Wang Jun of Luoyang, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, an excellent melon with separate bodies on one stem grew in the garden of Wang Jun, Supporting-State General of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康元年十二月戊子，嘉瓠生寧州，寧州刺史費統以聞。

translations.literal: On the wuzi day of the twelfth month of the first year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, an excellent gourd grew in Ning Province; the Inspector of Ningzhou Fei Tong reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day of the twelfth month of the first year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, an excellent gourd appeared in Ning Province, and Fei Tong, Inspector of Ningzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十五年四月戊辰，嘉瓠生京邑新園，園丞徐道興以獻。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, an excellent gourd grew in the New Park of the capital; the park director Xu Daoxing presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, an excellent gourd grew in the New Park of the capital, and Park Director Xu Daoxing presented it.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明五年五月，嘉瓜生建康蔣陵里，丹陽尹王僧朗以獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, an excellent melon grew in Jianglingli, Jiankang; the Prefect of Danyang Wang Sillang presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, an excellent melon grew in Jianglingli in Jiankang, and Wang Sillang, Prefect of Danyang, presented it.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始二年八月戊午，嘉瓜生南豫州，南豫州刺史山陽王休祐以獻。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day of the eighth month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, an excellent melon grew in South Yuzhou; the Inspector of South Yuzhou, the Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the eighth month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, an excellent melon appeared in South Yuzhou, and Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang and Inspector of South Yuzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉七年七月乙酉，建康頟檐湖二蓮一蔕。

translations.literal: On the yiyou day of the seventh month of the seventh year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, in the Eshan Lake of Jiankang two lotuses shared one stem.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the seventh month of the seventh year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, two lotuses on one stem appeared in Eshan Lake in Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十六年七月壬申，華林池雙蓮同榦。

translations.literal: On the renshen day of the seventh month of the sixteenth year of Yuanjia, in the Hualin Pool twin lotuses shared one stalk.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day of the seventh month of the sixteenth year of Yuanjia, twin lotuses on one stalk appeared in Hualin Pool.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十年七月己丑，華林天淵池芙蓉異花同蔕。

translations.literal: On the jichou day of the seventh month of the tenth year of Yuanjia, in the Hualin Celestial Abyss Pool lotus flowers of unusual form shared one stem.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day of the seventh month of the tenth year of Yuanjia, unusual lotus flowers on one stem appeared in the Celestial Abyss Pool in Hualin.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十九年八月壬子，揚州後池二蓮合華，刺史始興王濬以獻。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the eighth month of the nineteenth year of Yuanjia, in the rear pool of Yangzhou two lotuses joined in bloom; the Inspector, the Prince of Shixing Jun, presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the eighth month of the nineteenth year of Yuanjia, two lotuses bloomed together in the rear pool of Yangzhou, and Jun, Prince of Shixing and provincial inspector, presented them.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年五月，廬陵郡池芙蓉二花一蔕，太守王淵以聞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, in the pool of Luling Commandery two lotus flowers shared one stem; the grand administrator Wang Yuan reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, two lotus flowers on one stem appeared in the pool of Luling Commandery, and Grand Administrator Wang Yuan reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年六月壬寅，華林天淵池芙蓉二花一蔕，園丞陳襲祖以聞。

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the sixth month of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, in the Hualin Celestial Abyss Pool two lotus flowers shared one stem; the park director Chen Xizu reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day of the sixth month of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, two lotus flowers on one stem appeared in the Celestial Abyss Pool in Hualin, and Park Director Chen Xizu reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年夏，永嘉郡後池芙蓉二花一蔕，太守臧藝以聞。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, in the rear pool of Yongjia Commandery two lotus flowers shared one stem; the grand administrator Zang Yi reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, two lotus flowers on one stem appeared in the rear pool of Yongjia Commandery, and Grand Administrator Zang Yi reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年七月，吳興郡後池芙蓉二花一蔕，太守孔山士以聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, in the rear pool of Wuxing Commandery two lotus flowers shared one stem; the grand administrator Kong Shanshi reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, two lotus flowers on one stem appeared in the rear pool of Wuxing Commandery, and Grand Administrator Kong Shanshi reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年，揚州後池芙蓉二花一蔕，刺史始興王濬以獻。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Yuanjia, in the rear pool of Yangzhou two lotus flowers shared one stem; the Inspector, the Prince of Shixing Jun, presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Yuanjia, two lotus flowers on one stem appeared in the rear pool of Yangzhou, and Jun, Prince of Shixing and provincial inspector, presented them.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十一年六月丙午，華林園天淵池二蓮同榦，園丞陳襲祖以聞。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day of the sixth month of the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, in the Celestial Abyss Pool of Hualin Park two lotuses shared one stalk; the park director Chen Xizu reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day of the sixth month of the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, two lotuses on one stalk appeared in the Celestial Abyss Pool of Hualin Park, and Park Director Chen Xizu reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年四月，樂游苑池二蓮同榦，苑丞梅道念以聞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, in the pool of the Leyou Park two lotuses shared one stalk; the park director Mei Daonian reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, two lotuses on one stalk appeared in the pool of Leyou Park, and Park Director Mei Daonian reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年七月，東宮玄圃園池二蓮同榦，內監殿守舍人宮勇民以聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, in the pool of the Eastern Palace Mystic Garden two lotuses shared one stalk; the inner attendant palace guard gentleman Gong Yongmin reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, two lotuses on one stalk appeared in the pool of the Mystic Garden of the Eastern Palace, and Inner Attendant Palace Guard Gentleman Gong Yongmin reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十三年六月壬寅，華林天淵池芙蓉二花一蔕，園丞陳襲祖以聞。

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the sixth month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, in the Hualin Celestial Abyss Pool two lotus flowers shared one stem; the park director Chen Xizu reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day of the sixth month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, two lotus flowers on one stem appeared in the Celestial Abyss Pool in Hualin, and Park Director Chen Xizu reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十三年六月辛丑，太子西池二蓮共榦，池統胡永祖以聞。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day of the sixth month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, in the Crown Prince's western pool two lotuses shared one stalk; the pool supervisor Hu Yongzu reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the sixth month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, two lotuses on one stalk appeared in the Crown Prince's western pool, and Pool Supervisor Hu Yongzu reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十三年八月己酉，魚邑三周池二蓮同榦，園丞徐道興以聞。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day of the eighth month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, in the Sanzhou Pool of Yuyi two lotuses shared one stalk; the park director Xu Daoxing reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the eighth month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, two lotuses on one stalk appeared in the Sanzhou Pool of Yuyi, and Park Director Xu Daoxing reported it.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝孝建二年六月庚寅，玄武湖二蓮同榦。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the sixth month of the second year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiao of Song, in Xuanwu Lake two lotuses shared one stalk.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the sixth month of the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiao of Song, two lotuses on one stalk appeared in Xuanwu Lake.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明五年，籍田芙蓉二花同蔕，大司農蕭邃以獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, in the sacred plow fields two lotus flowers shared one stem; the Minister of Revenue Xiao Sui presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, two lotus flowers on one stem appeared in the sacred plow fields, and Minister of Revenue Xiao Sui presented them.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始二年八月丙辰，五城澳池二蓮同榦，都水使者羅僧愍以獻。

translations.literal: On the bingchen day of the eighth month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, in the Wucheng Ao Pool two lotuses shared one stalk; the Commissioner of Waterways Luo Songmin presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day of the eighth month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, two lotuses on one stalk appeared in the Wucheng Ao Pool, and Commissioner of Waterways Luo Songmin presented them.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年八月己未，豫州刺史山陽王休祐獻蓮，二花一蔕。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day of the eighth month of the second year of Taishi, the Inspector of Yuzhou, the Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou, presented lotuses—two flowers on one stem.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day of the eighth month of the second year of Taishi, Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang and Inspector of Yuzhou, presented lotuses with two flowers on one stem.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年六月甲子，嘉蓮生湖熟，南臺侍御史竺曾度以聞。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Taishi, excellent lotuses grew in Hushu; the Attending Censor of the Southern Bureau Zhu Zengdu reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Taishi, excellent lotuses appeared in Hushu, and Zhu Zengdu, Attending Censor of the Southern Bureau, reported it.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年六月壬子，嘉蓮生東宮玄圃池，皇太子以聞。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the sixth month of the sixth year of Taishi, excellent lotuses grew in the Mystic Garden Pool of the Eastern Palace; the Crown Prince reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the sixth month of the sixth year of Taishi, excellent lotuses grew in the Mystic Garden Pool of the Eastern Palace, and the Crown Prince reported it.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始二年六月壬申，嘉柰一蔕十實，生酒泉。

translations.literal: On the renshen day of the sixth month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, an excellent nai with one stem and ten fruits grew in Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day of the sixth month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, an excellent nai with one stem and ten fruits grew in Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年六月己亥，東宮玄圃池芙蓉二花一蔕，皇太子以獻。

translations.literal: On the jihai day of the sixth month of the seventh year of Taishi, in the Mystic Garden Pool of the Eastern Palace two lotus flowers shared one stem; the Crown Prince presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the sixth month of the seventh year of Taishi, two lotus flowers on one stem appeared in the Mystic Garden Pool of the Eastern Palace, and the Crown Prince presented them.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和六年，鎮西將軍庾亮獻嘉橘，一蔕十二實。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin, the General Who Pacifies the West Yu Liang presented an excellent orange—one stem with twelve fruits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng of Jin, Yu Liang, General Who Pacifies the West, presented an excellent orange with one stem and twelve fruits.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安三年，武陵臨沅獻安石榴，一蔕六實。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longan of Emperor An of Jin, Linyuan in Wuling presented a peaceful pomegranate—one stem with six fruits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Longan under Emperor An of Jin, Linyuan in Wuling presented a peaceful pomegranate with one stem and six fruits.

sentences.zh: 雲有五色

translations.literal: Clouds have five colors
translations.idiomatic: Clouds have five colors

sentences.zh: 雲有五色，太平之應也，曰慶雲。

translations.literal: Clouds have five colors—it is a response of great peace, called the celebratory cloud.
translations.idiomatic: When clouds have five colors, it is a sign of great peace and is called the celebratory cloud.

sentences.zh: 若雲非雲，若煙非煙，五色紛縕，謂之慶雲。

translations.literal: Like cloud yet not cloud, like smoke yet not smoke, five colors interwoven—this is called the celebratory cloud.
translations.idiomatic: Like cloud yet not cloud, like smoke yet not smoke, with five colors interwoven—this is called the celebratory cloud.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝神爵四年春，齋戒之莫，神光顯著。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Shenjue of Emperor Xuan of Han, at the end of the fasting period, divine light was conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year of Shenjue under Emperor Xuan of Han, at the close of the fasting period, divine light appeared in plain sight.

sentences.zh: 薦鬯之夕，神光交錯，或降于天，或登于地，或從四方，來集于壇上。

translations.literal: On the evening of offering fragrant spirits, divine light crossed and interwove—sometimes descending from Heaven, sometimes rising from earth, sometimes coming from the four directions to gather on the altar.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening of offering fragrant spirits, divine light crossed and interwove, sometimes descending from Heaven, sometimes rising from the earth, sometimes coming from the four directions to gather upon the altar.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和三年正月，車駕北巡，以太牢祠北岳山，見黃白氣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Yuanhe of Emperor Zhang of Han, the imperial carriage toured north, sacrificed with the grand victim at Mount Beiyue, and yellow-white vapor was seen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Yuanhe under Emperor Zhang of Han, the emperor toured north, offered the grand sacrifice at Mount Beiyue, and yellow-white vapor appeared.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武帝大明元年五月壬子，紫氣從景陽樓上層出，狀如煙，回薄良久。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the fifth month of the first year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, purple vapor emerged from the upper story of Jingyang Tower, shaped like smoke, swirling and lingering for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the fifth month of the first year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, purple vapor rose from the upper story of Jingyang Tower like smoke, swirling and lingering for a long while.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始二年三月丙午，黃紫雲從景陽樓出，隨風回，久乃消，華林園令臧延之以聞。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day of the third month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, yellow-purple clouds emerged from Jingyang Tower, turned with the wind, and only after a long time vanished; the Director of Hualin Park Zang Yanzhi reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day of the third month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, yellow-purple clouds rose from Jingyang Tower, turned with the wind, and lingered long before fading; Zang Yanzhi, Director of Hualin Park, reported it.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年六月己卯，日入後，有黃白赤白氣東西竟天，光明潤澤，久乃消。

translations.literal: On the jimao day of the sixth month of the second year of Taishi, after sunset, yellow-white and red-white vapors stretched east and west across the sky, bright and lustrous, and only after a long time vanished.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day of the sixth month of the second year of Taishi, after sunset, yellow-white and red-white vapors stretched from east to west across the sky, bright and lustrous, and lingered long before fading.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年十一月辛未，崇寧陵令上書言，自大明八年至今四年二月，宣太后陵明堂前後數有光及五色雲，又芳香四滿，又五采雲在松下，狀如車蓋。

translations.literal: On the xinwei day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Taishi, the director of Chongning Mausoleum submitted a memorial saying that from the eighth year of Daming until now—four years and two months—the tomb of Empress Dowager Xuan before and after the Bright Hall had repeatedly had light and five-colored clouds, fragrance filling on all four sides, and a five-colored cloud under a pine tree shaped like a carriage canopy.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Taishi, the director of Chongning Mausoleum submitted a memorial stating that from the eighth year of Daming until then—four years and two months—the area before and after the Bright Hall at Empress Dowager Xuan's tomb had repeatedly shown light and five-colored clouds, fragrance on every side, and a five-colored cloud beneath a pine shaped like a carriage canopy.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年四月戊申夜，京邑崇虛館堂前有黃氣，狀如寶蓋，高十許丈，漸有五色，道士陸脩靜以聞。

translations.literal: On the night of the wushen day of the fourth month of the seventh year of Taishi, before the hall of Chongxu Lodge in the capital there was yellow vapor shaped like a jeweled canopy, about ten zhang high, gradually taking on five colors; the Daoist Lu Xiujing reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the wushen day of the fourth month of the seventh year of Taishi, yellow vapor shaped like a jeweled canopy, about ten zhang high and gradually suffused with five colors, appeared before the hall of Chongxu Lodge in the capital, and the Daoist Lu Xiujing reported it.

sentences.zh: 白兔

translations.literal: White Rabbit
translations.idiomatic: White Rabbit

sentences.zh: 白兔，王者敬耆老則見。

translations.literal: The white rabbit—when a king reveres the aged, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler reveres the elderly, white rabbits appear.

sentences.zh: 漢光武建武十三年九月，南越獻白兔。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Jianwu of Emperor Guangwu of Han, Nanyue presented a white rabbit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Jianwu under Emperor Guangwu of Han, Nanyue presented a white rabbit.

sentences.zh: 章帝元和中，白兔見郡國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang, white rabbits appeared in the commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era under Emperor Zhang of Han, white rabbits appeared in the commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初中，郡國十九言白兔見。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu era of Emperor Wen of Wei, nineteen commanderies and kingdoms reported white rabbits appearing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangchu era under Emperor Wen of Wei, nineteen commanderies and kingdoms reported white rabbits.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始五年七月己亥，白兔見北海即墨，即墨長獲以獻。

translations.literal: On the jihai day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, a white rabbit appeared at Jimo in Beihai; the magistrate of Jimo captured it and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, a white rabbit appeared at Jimo in Beihai, and the magistrate of Jimo captured and presented it.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧二年十月癸亥，白兔二見河南陽翟，陽翟令華衍獲以獻。

translations.literal: On the guihai day of the tenth month of the second year of Xianning of Emperor Wu of Jin, two white rabbits appeared at Yangzhai in Henan; the magistrate of Yangzhai Hua Yan captured them and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day of the tenth month of the second year of Xianning under Emperor Wu of Jin, two white rabbits appeared at Yangzhai in Henan, and Hua Yan, magistrate of Yangzhai, captured and presented them.

sentences.zh: 咸寧四年六月，白兔見天水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Xianning, a white rabbit appeared in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Xianning, a white rabbit appeared in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康二年八月壬子，白兔見彭城。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the eighth month of the second year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, a white rabbit appeared in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the eighth month of the second year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, a white rabbit appeared in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 太康二年十月，白兔見趙國平鄉，趙王倫獲以獻。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Taikang, a white rabbit appeared at Pingxiang in Zhao Commandery; the Prince of Zhao Lun captured it and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Taikang, a white rabbit appeared at Pingxiang in Zhao Commandery, and Prince Lun of Zhao captured and presented it.

sentences.zh: 太康四年十一月癸未，白兔見北地富平。

translations.literal: On the guiwei day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Taikang, a white rabbit appeared at Fuping in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Taikang, a white rabbit appeared at Fuping in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 太康八年十二月庚戌，白兔見陳留酸棗，關內侯成公忠獲以獻。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day of the twelfth month of the eighth year of Taikang, a white rabbit appeared at Suanzao in Chenliu; the Marquis within the Passes Cheng Gongzhong captured it and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the twelfth month of the eighth year of Taikang, a white rabbit appeared at Suanzao in Chenliu, and Cheng Gongzhong, Marquis within the Passes, captured and presented it.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和十二年九月甲申，白兔見鄱陽，太守王耆之以獻，并上頌一篇。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day of the ninth month of the twelfth year of Yonghe of Emperor Mu of Jin, a white rabbit appeared in Poyang; the grand administrator Wang Qizhi presented it and also submitted a eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the ninth month of the twelfth year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu of Jin, a white rabbit appeared in Poyang; Wang Qizhi, grand administrator of Poyang, presented it and also submitted a eulogy.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝升平三年十二月庚申，北中郎將郗曇獻白兔。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day of the twelfth month of the third year of Shengping of Emperor Mu of Jin, the General of the North Zhonglang Xi Tan presented a white rabbit.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the twelfth month of the third year of Shengping under Emperor Mu of Jin, Xi Tan, General of the North Zhonglang, presented a white rabbit.

sentences.zh: 晉海西公太和九年四月，陽穀獻白兔。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Taihe of Emperor Haixi of Jin, Yanggu presented a white rabbit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Taihe under Emperor Haixi of Jin, Yanggu presented a white rabbit.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元十五年三月，白兔見淮南壽陽。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, a white rabbit appeared at Shouyang in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifteenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, a white rabbit appeared at Shouyang in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙二年四月，無錫獻白兔。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin, Wuxi presented a white rabbit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, Wuxi presented a white rabbit.

sentences.zh: 義熙二年四月，壽陽獻白兔。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yixi, Shouyang presented a white rabbit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Yixi, Shouyang presented a white rabbit.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉六年九月，長廣昌陽淳于邈獲白兔，青州刺史蕭思話以獻。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, Chunyu Miao of Changyang in Changguang captured a white rabbit; the Inspector of Qingzhou Xiao Sihua presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, Chunyu Miao of Changyang in Changguang captured a white rabbit, and Xiao Sihua, Inspector of Qingzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉八年閏六月丁亥，司徒府白從伊生於淮南繁昌獲白兔以獻。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day of the intercalary sixth month of the eighth year of Yuanjia, Bai Congyi, an attendant of the Minister of Works office, captured a white rabbit at Fanchang in Huainan and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the intercalary sixth month of the eighth year of Yuanjia, Bai Congyi, an attendant of the Minister of Works office, captured a white rabbit at Fanchang in Huainan and presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十三年七月甲戌，濟南朝陽王道獲白兔，青州刺史段宏以獻。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day of the seventh month of the thirteenth year of Yuanjia, the Prince of Chaoyang Dao of Jijun captured a white rabbit; the Inspector of Qingzhou Duan Hong presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day of the seventh month of the thirteenth year of Yuanjia, Dao, Prince of Chaoyang in Jijun, captured a white rabbit, and Duan Hong, Inspector of Qingzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十四年正月丙申，白兔見山陽縣，山陽太守劉懷之以獻。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day of the first month of the fourteenth year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared in Shanyang County; the grand administrator of Shanyang Liu Huaizhi presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the first month of the fourteenth year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared in Shanyang County, and Liu Huaizhi, grand administrator of Shanyang, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十五年七月壬申，山陽師齊獲白兔，南兗州刺史江夏王義恭以獻。

translations.literal: On the renshen day of the seventh month of the fifteenth year of Yuanjia, Shi Qi of Shanyang captured a white rabbit; the Inspector of South Yanzhou, the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day of the seventh month of the fifteenth year of Yuanjia, Shi Qi of Shanyang captured a white rabbit, and Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia and Inspector of South Yanzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年三月，白兔見東萊當利，青州刺史杜驥以聞。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared at Dangli in Donglai; the Inspector of Qingzhou Du Ji reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared at Dangli in Donglai, and Du Ji, Inspector of Qingzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十四年七月丁巳，白兔見兗州，刺史徐瓊以聞。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day of the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared in Yan Province; the Inspector Xu Qiong reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared in Yan Province, and Xu Qiong, Inspector of Yanzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十四年七月己酉，白兔見東莞，太守趙球以獻。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day of the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared in Dongguan; the grand administrator Zhao Qiu presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared in Dongguan, and Zhao Qiu, grand administrator of Dongguan, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年二月壬辰，白兔見竟陵，荊州刺史南譙王義宣以獻。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the second month of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared in Jingling; the Inspector of Jingzhou, the Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the second month of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared in Jingling, and Yixuan, Prince of Nanqiao and Inspector of Jingzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年六月丙午，白兔見南汝陰，豫州刺史南平王鑠以獻。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day of the sixth month of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared in South Ruyin; the Inspector of Yuzhou, the Prince of Nanping Shuo, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day of the sixth month of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, a white rabbit appeared in South Ruyin, and Shuo, Prince of Nanping and Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝孝建二年正月庚戌，白兔見淮南，太守申坦以聞。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day of the first month of the second year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiao of Song, a white rabbit appeared in Huainan; the grand administrator Shen Tan reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the first month of the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiao of Song, a white rabbit appeared in Huainan, and Shen Tan, grand administrator of Huainan, reported it.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年閏三月乙丑，白兔見平原，獲以獻。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the intercalary third month of the third year of Xiaojian, a white rabbit appeared in Pingyuan; it was captured and presented.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the intercalary third month of the third year of Xiaojian, a white rabbit appeared in Pingyuan, was captured, and was presented.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明元年六月庚子，白兔見即墨，獲以獻。
