sentences.zh: 白鳩

translations.literal: White Dove
translations.idiomatic: White Dove

sentences.zh: 白鳩，成湯時來至。

translations.literal: The white dove arrived in the time of King Cheng Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The white dove came in the age of King Cheng Tang.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初初，郡國十九言白鳩見。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huangchu era of Emperor Wen of Wei, nineteen commanderies and kingdoms reported that white doves had appeared.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huangchu era under Emperor Wen of Wei, nineteen commanderies and kingdoms reported the appearance of white doves.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權赤烏十二年八月癸丑，白鳩見章安。

translations.literal: On the guichou day of the eighth month of the twelfth year of Chiwu of Sun Quan of Wu, a white dove appeared in Zhang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day of the eighth month of the twelfth year of Chiwu under Sun Quan of Wu, a white dove appeared in Zhang'an.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始八年五月甲辰，白鳩二集太廟南門，議郎董冑獲以獻。

translations.literal: On the jiachen day of the fifth month of the eighth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, two white doves gathered at the south gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Dong Zhou, Gentleman Consultant, captured them and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the fifth month of the eighth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, two white doves gathered at the south gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and Dong Zhou, Gentleman Consultant, captured and presented them.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康二年七月，白鳩見太僕寺。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, a white dove appeared at the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, a white dove appeared at the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 太康四年十二月，白鳩見安定臨涇。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Taikang, a white dove appeared at Linyuan in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Taikang, a white dove appeared at Linyuan in Anding.

sentences.zh: 太康十年正月乙亥，白鳩見河南新城。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the first month of the tenth year of Taikang, a white dove appeared in Xincheng, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the first month of the tenth year of Taikang, a white dove appeared in Xincheng in Henan.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十八年八月庚午，會稽山陰商世寶獲白鳩，眼足並赤，揚州刺史始興王濬以獻。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day of the eighth month of the eighteenth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, Shang Shibao of Shanyin in Kuaiji captured a white dove with both eyes and feet red; the Inspector of Yangzhou, the Prince of Shixing Jun, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the eighth month of the eighteenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, Shang Shibao of Shanyin in Kuaiji captured a white dove whose eyes and feet were both red, and Jun, Prince of Shixing and Inspector of Yangzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 太子率更令何承天上表曰：

translations.literal: He Chengtian, Director of the Crown Prince's Household Administration, submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian, Director of the Crown Prince's Household Administration, submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: :謹考尋先典，稽之前志，王德所覃，物以應顯。

translations.literal: I respectfully examine the ancient canons and verify against earlier records: where royal virtue extends, things respond by manifesting.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully examining the ancient canons and verifying against earlier chronicles, I find that where royal virtue spreads abroad, things respond by manifesting themselves.

sentences.zh: 是以玄扈之鳳，昭帝軒之鴻烈，酆宮之雀，徵姬文之徽祚。

translations.literal: Hence the phoenix of Xuanhu displayed the great merit of the Yellow Emperor, and the sparrow at Feng marked the blessed fortune of King Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the phoenix of Xuanhu proclaimed the glorious achievement of the Yellow Emperor, and the sparrow at the Feng altar betokened the blessed fortune of King Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下重光嗣服，永言祖武，洽惠和於地絡，燭皇明於天區。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty has renewed the imperial light and succeeded to the throne, ever speaking of ancestral martial prowess, spreading benevolence and harmony through the earthly realm, and illuminating imperial brilliance across the celestial region.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty has renewed the imperial radiance and inherited the throne, ever mindful of ancestral martial achievement, spreading grace and harmony through the realm and shining imperial brilliance across the heavens.

sentences.zh: 故能九服混心，萬邦含愛，圓神降祥，方祇薦裕，休珍雜沓，景瑞畢臻。

translations.literal: Thus the nine domains are of one mind, the myriad states cherish compassion, the circular spirit sends down blessings, the square earth offers abundance, auspicious treasures come in profusion, and brilliant omens all arrive.
translations.idiomatic: By this the nine domains are united in heart, the myriad states embrace your benevolence, the spirit of Heaven sends down blessings, the spirit of Earth offers its bounty, auspicious treasures arrive in abundance, and brilliant omens all appear.

sentences.zh: 去七月上旬，時在昧旦，黃暉洞照，宇宙開朗，徽風協律，甘液灑津。

translations.literal: In the first ten days of the seventh month past, at the hour of dawn, golden radiance penetrated and illumined all; the universe opened bright; the subtle wind harmonized with the pitch pipes; sweet dew sprinkled the ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the first third of the seventh month past, at dawn, golden light filled the universe and all was bright; a gentle wind matched the pitch pipes, and sweet dew fell upon the land.

sentences.zh: 雖朱晃瑰瑋於運衡，榮光圖靈於河紀，蔑以尚茲。

translations.literal: Though the vermilion radiance was rare and precious at the Transport Pivot, and gloriously patterned spirits appeared on the River's record, none could surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Though the vermilion glory was marvelous at the celestial pivot, and glorious spirits were inscribed upon the river's chronicle, none could exceed what we now behold.

sentences.zh: 臣不量卑懵，竊慕擊壤有作，相杵成謳。

translations.literal: Your subject, not measuring his low ignorance, secretly admires those who struck the earth and made songs, beating pestles together to form hymns.
translations.idiomatic: I do not weigh my lowly ignorance, but secretly admire the ancients who struck the earth in song, beating their pestles together to make hymns.

sentences.zh: 近又豫白鳩之觀，目翫奇偉，心歡盛烈。

translations.literal: Recently I again witnessed the white dove; my eyes delighted in its marvelous grandeur, and my heart rejoiced in its splendid majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I once more beheld the white dove; my eyes took joy in its wondrous form, and my heart rejoiced in the grandeur of this sign.

sentences.zh: 謹獻頌一篇。

translations.literal: I respectfully present an encomium in one piece.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit an encomium in one piece.

sentences.zh: 野思古拙，意及庸陋，不足以發揮清英，敷讚幽旨，瞻前顧後，亦各其志。

translations.literal: My rustic thoughts are antiquated and blunt, my meaning reaches only to the vulgar and plain; it is not enough to unfold the pure brilliance or spread forth praise of the hidden intent; looking before and after, each also follows his own purpose.
translations.idiomatic: My rustic thoughts are crude and antiquated, my meaning barely rises above the commonplace; they are insufficient to unfold pure brilliance or proclaim the hidden truth. Looking to those before and after me, each has followed his own intent.

sentences.zh: 謹冒以聞。

translations.literal: I respectfully take the liberty of reporting this.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully take the liberty of reporting this to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 其白鳩頌曰：

translations.literal: The hymn to the white dove reads:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn to the white dove reads:

sentences.zh: :三極協情，五靈會性。

translations.literal: The three poles harmonize in sentiment; the five numina gather in nature.
translations.idiomatic: The three cosmic poles share one sentiment; the five numina unite in their essence.

sentences.zh: 理感冥符，道實玄聖。

translations.literal: Principle responds in dark correspondence; the Way is truly mysterious and sacred.
translations.idiomatic: Principle responds in hidden correspondence; the Way truly manifests as the sacred sage.

sentences.zh: 於赫有皇，光天配命。

translations.literal: Oh, glorious is the sovereign; he illumines Heaven and matches the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Glorious is the sovereign, who illumines Heaven and fulfills the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 朝景升躔，八維同映。

translations.literal: Morning radiance ascends the celestial steps; the eight dimensions all reflect together.
translations.idiomatic: Morning light climbs the sky's steps, and the eight directions reflect as one.

sentences.zh: 休祥載臻，榮光播慶。

translations.literal: Auspicious omens arrive in succession; honor and glory spread celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Blessed omens arrive in succession, and glory and joy spread abroad.

sentences.zh: 宇宙照爛，日月光華。

translations.literal: The cosmos shines brilliantly; sun and moon shed glory.
translations.idiomatic: The cosmos blazes with light; sun and moon pour forth their brilliance.

sentences.zh: 陶山練澤，是生柔嘉。

translations.literal: Pottery Mountain, refined marsh—there grows soft excellence.
translations.idiomatic: From Pottery Mountain and the refined marshes springs soft excellence.

sentences.zh: 回龍表粹，離穗合柯。

translations.literal: The turning dragon displays pure essence; separated ears share branches.
translations.idiomatic: The turning dragon reveals pure essence; separate ears share one stem.

sentences.zh: 翩翩者鳩，亦皎其暉。

translations.literal: Fluttering is the dove, also bright its radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Fluttering is the dove, its radiance bright and clear.

sentences.zh: 理翮台領，揚鮮帝畿。

translations.literal: It puts in order its wings at the terrace crest, spreading freshness through the Imperial Domain.
translations.idiomatic: It arranges its wings on the terrace crest and spreads its brightness through the Imperial Domain.

sentences.zh: 匪仁莫集，匪德莫歸。

translations.literal: Without benevolence none gather; without virtue none return.
translations.idiomatic: Without benevolence none congregate; without virtue none return.

sentences.zh: 暮從儀鳳，棲閣廕闈。

translations.literal: At dusk it follows the ceremonial phoenix, roosting in the pavilion sheltered by the inner gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk it follows the ceremonial phoenix, roosting in the pavilion beneath the inner gate's shelter.

sentences.zh: :烝哉明后，昧旦乾乾。

translations.literal: How abundant is the wise sovereign, rising at dawn and striving diligently.
translations.idiomatic: How abundant is the wise sovereign, rising at dawn and striving earnestly.

sentences.zh: 惟德之崇，其峻如山。

translations.literal: Only virtue's loftiness—it is steep as mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Only his virtue stands lofty, as steep as mountains.

sentences.zh: 惟澤之贍，其潤如淵。

translations.literal: Only grace's bounty—it is moist as deep pools.
translations.idiomatic: Only his grace is bountiful, as moist as deep pools.

sentences.zh: 禮樂四達，頌聲遐宣。

translations.literal: Rites and music reach the four quarters; eulogistic sounds spread far.
translations.idiomatic: Rites and music reach the four quarters, and songs of praise resound afar.

sentences.zh: 窮髮納貢，九譯導言。

translations.literal: Remote borderlands submit tribute; nine-fold translation guides the speech.
translations.idiomatic: Lands at the ends of the earth bring tribute; interpreters through nine tongues convey their words.

sentences.zh: 伊昔唐萌，愛逢慶祚。

translations.literal: Long ago Old Tang cherished encountering blessed fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Old Tang cherished meeting blessed fortune.

sentences.zh: 余生既辰，而年之暮。

translations.literal: My remaining life reached the appointed hour, yet the year is at its end.
translations.idiomatic: My remaining years have reached their season, yet life is in its evening.

sentences.zh: 提心命耋，式歌王度。

translations.literal: I lift my heart, my life at old age, and sing the king's measure.
translations.idiomatic: With heart uplifted in my old age, I chant the king's governance.

sentences.zh: 晨晞永風，夕漱甘露。

translations.literal: Morning bathes in the eternal wind; evening rinses with sweet dew.
translations.idiomatic: Morning I bathe in the eternal wind; evening I rinse with sweet dew.

sentences.zh: 思樂靈臺，不遐有固。

translations.literal: Longing joy for the Spirit Terrace—not far, truly fixed.
translations.idiomatic: I long for joy at the Spirit Terrace—not far off, with enduring foundation.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十四年九月，白鳩又見。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, a white dove again appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, a white dove appeared again.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，中領軍沈演之上表曰：

translations.literal: On the gengxu day, Shen Yanzhi, Central Palace Guard General, submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, Shen Yanzhi, Central Palace Guard General, submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: :臣聞貞裕之美，介於盛王，休瑞之臻，罔違哲后。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the beauty of constancy and bounty lies between prosperous kings; the arrival of auspicious omens never fails a wise sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the beauty of constancy and bounty belongs to flourishing kings, and that auspicious omens never fail to attend a wise sovereign.

sentences.zh: 故鳴鳳表垂衣之化，翔鷦徵解網之仁。

translations.literal: Hence the singing phoenix displayed the transformation of ruling through non-interference; the soaring wren marked the benevolence of releasing the net.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the singing phoenix displayed the rule of effortless governance, and the soaring wren marked the benevolence of releasing the net.

sentences.zh: 陛下道德嗣基，聖明纘世，教清鳥紀，治昌雲官，禮漸同川，澤浹朱徼。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's virtue and the Way succeed the foundation, sagely clarity continues the age; instruction clears the bird calendar, governance flourishes at the cloud offices; rites spread like a river, grace saturates the vermilion frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue and the Way carry on the foundation, and sagely clarity continues the age; instruction clears the bird calendar, governance flourishes among the cloud offices, rites spread like a river, and grace saturates the vermilion frontier.

sentences.zh: 天嘉明懿，民樂薰風，星辰以之炳煥，日月以之光華。

translations.literal: Heaven approves clear virtue; the people rejoice in the scented wind; stars by this blaze bright, sun and moon by this shed glory.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven approves clear virtue, the people rejoice in the scented wind, the stars blaze bright by this, and sun and moon shed glory by this.

sentences.zh: 神圖祇緯，盈觀閟序，白質黑章，充牣靈囿。

translations.literal: Divine charts and sacred omens fill the palace halls; white body and black markings fill the spirit park.
translations.idiomatic: Divine charts and sacred omens fill the palace halls, and white body with black markings fill the spirit park.

sentences.zh: 應感之符畢臻，而因心之祥未屬。

translations.literal: Tokens of responsive sympathy all arrive, yet the omen born of inner sincerity has not yet attached.
translations.idiomatic: Tokens of responsive sympathy have all arrived, yet the omen born of inner sincerity has not yet been fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 以素鳩自遠，毨翰歸飛，資性閑淑，羽貌鮮麗，既聞之先說，又親覩嘉祥，不勝藻抃，上頌一首。

translations.literal: Because the plain dove came from afar, colored wings returning in flight, its nature refined and virtuous, plumage bright and lovely—having heard the earlier accounts and now personally witnessing this blessed omen, unable to contain my literary joy, I submit an encomium in one piece.
translations.idiomatic: The plain dove came from afar, its colored wings returning in flight; its nature is refined and virtuous, its plumage bright and lovely. Having heard the earlier accounts and now personally witnessing this blessed omen, I cannot contain my literary joy and submit an encomium in one piece.

sentences.zh: 辭不稽典，文乏采章，愧不足式昭皇慶，崇讚盛美，蓋率輿誦，備之篇末。

translations.literal: My words do not consult the classics; my text lacks ornament—ashamed it is not enough to model imperial celebration or exalt splendid beauty; I simply follow what the people chant and place it at the end of the chapter.
translations.idiomatic: My words do not consult the classics, and my text lacks ornament; I am ashamed that it is not enough to model imperial celebration or exalt splendid beauty. I simply follow what the people chant and place it at the end of the chapter.

sentences.zh: 其頌曰：

translations.literal: The hymn reads:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

sentences.zh: :有哲其儀，時惟皓鳩。

translations.literal: Wise is its bearing; the white dove of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wise is its bearing—the white dove of the age.

sentences.zh: 性勰五教，名編素丘。

translations.literal: Its nature harmonizes with the five teachings; its name is enrolled at the Plain Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Its nature harmonizes with the five teachings, and its name is enrolled at the Plain Mound.

sentences.zh: 殷曆方昌，婉翹來遊。

translations.literal: The Yin calendar is flourishing; gracefully it comes to roam.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin calendar is flourishing, and gracefully it comes to roam.

sentences.zh: 漢錄克韡，爰降爰休。

translations.literal: The Han records were splendid; then it descended, then it rested.
translations.idiomatic: The Han records were splendid; then it descended, then it rested.

sentences.zh: 〈其一〉

translations.literal: 〈One〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈One〉

sentences.zh: 於顯盛宋，叡慶遐傳。

translations.literal: Oh, glorious Song; wise blessing spreads far.
translations.idiomatic: Oh, glorious Song; wise blessing spreads far.

sentences.zh: 聖皇在上，道照鴻軒。

translations.literal: The sacred sovereign is above; the Way illumines the vast carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred sovereign reigns above, and the Way illumines the vast carriage.

sentences.zh: 稱施既平，孝思永言。

translations.literal: His bestowals are already even; filial thought is ever spoken.
translations.idiomatic: His bestowals are already even, and filial thought is ever spoken.

sentences.zh: 人和於地，神豫于天。

translations.literal: People harmonize on earth; spirits rejoice in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: People harmonize on earth, and spirits rejoice in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 〈其二〉

translations.literal: 〈Two〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Two〉

sentences.zh: 禮樂孔秩，靈物咸昭。

translations.literal: Rites and music are well ordered; numinous things all manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Rites and music are well ordered, and numinous things all manifest.

sentences.zh: 白雀集苞，丹鳳棲郊。

translations.literal: White sparrows gather on buds; red phoenixes roost in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: White sparrows gather on buds, and red phoenixes roost in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 文騶儷跡，嘉穎擢苗。

translations.literal: Patterned zebras tread in pairs; excellent grain heads rise from seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: Patterned zebras tread in pairs, and excellent grain heads rise from seedlings.

sentences.zh: 灼灼縞羽，從化馴朝。

translations.literal: Bright white-striped wings follow transformation and tame the court.
translations.idiomatic: Bright white-striped wings follow transformation and tame the court.

sentences.zh: 〈其三〉

translations.literal: 〈Three〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Three〉

sentences.zh: 豈伊赴林，必周之栩。

translations.literal: Must it go to the woods? Surely Zhou's catalpa.
translations.idiomatic: Must it go to the woods? Surely it is Zhou's catalpa.

sentences.zh: 豈伊歸義，必商之所。

translations.literal: Must it return to righteousness? Surely Shang's place.
translations.idiomatic: Must it return to righteousness? Surely it is Shang's place.

sentences.zh: 惟德是依，惟仁是處。

translations.literal: Only virtue is relied upon; only benevolence is dwelt in.
translations.idiomatic: Only virtue is relied upon; only benevolence is dwelt in.

sentences.zh: 育景陽嶽，濯姿帝宇。

translations.literal: Nourished at Mount Jingyang, it washes its form in the imperial domain.
translations.idiomatic: Nourished at Mount Jingyang, it washes its form in the imperial domain.

sentences.zh: 〈其四〉

translations.literal: 〈Four〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Four〉

sentences.zh: 刑曆頒興，理感迭通。

translations.literal: Penal codes and calendars are promulgated; principle and sympathy alternate in correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Penal codes and calendars are promulgated, and principle and sympathy alternate in correspondence.

sentences.zh: 雉飛越常，鷺起西雍。

translations.literal: Pheasants fly beyond the norm; egrets rise in Western Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Pheasants fly beyond the norm, and egrets rise in Western Yong.

sentences.zh: 烝然戾止，實兼斯容。

translations.literal: They arrive in multitude and settle; truly they combine this bearing.
translations.idiomatic: They arrive in multitude and settle, truly combining this bearing.

sentences.zh: 壹茲民聽，穆是王風。

translations.literal: Unifying this people's hearing, solemn is the king's wind.
translations.idiomatic: Unifying this people's hearing, solemn is the king's wind.

sentences.zh: 〈其五〉

translations.literal: 〈Five〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Five〉

sentences.zh: 玉羊

translations.literal: Jade Sheep
translations.idiomatic: Jade Sheep

sentences.zh: 玉羊，師曠時來至。

translations.literal: The jade sheep arrived in the time of Shi Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: The jade sheep appeared in the time of Shi Kuang.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 玉雞

translations.literal: Jade Rooster
translations.idiomatic: Jade Rooster

sentences.zh: 玉雞，王者至孝則至。

translations.literal: The jade rooster—when a king is supremely filial, it arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler is supremely filial, the jade rooster appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 璧流離

translations.literal: Glass Bi
translations.idiomatic: Glass Bi

sentences.zh: 璧流離，王者不隱過則至。

translations.literal: The glass bi—when a king does not conceal his faults, it arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler does not conceal his faults, the glass bi appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 玉英

translations.literal: Jade Splendor
translations.idiomatic: Jade Splendor

sentences.zh: 玉英，五常並修則見。

translations.literal: Jade splendor—when the five constants are all cultivated, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: When the five constants are all cultivated, jade splendor appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 玄圭

translations.literal: Dark Jade Tablet
translations.idiomatic: Dark Jade Tablet

sentences.zh: 玄圭，水泉流通，四海會同則出。

translations.literal: The dark jade tablet—when watercourses flow freely and the four seas unite, it emerges.
translations.idiomatic: When watercourses flow freely and the four seas unite, the dark jade tablet emerges.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝永興二年四月，光祿勳府吏舍，夜壁下有青氣，得玉鉤、玦各一。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yongxing of Emperor Huan of Han, at the clerks' quarters of the Household of the Minister of the Imperial Household, at night there was azure vapor beneath the wall, and one jade hook and one jade ring were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Yongxing under Emperor Huan of Han, at the clerks' quarters of the Household of the Minister of the Imperial Household, azure vapor appeared beneath the wall at night, and one jade hook and one jade ring were found.

sentences.zh: 鉤長七寸三分，玦周五寸四分，身中皆雕鏤。

translations.literal: The hook was seven cun and three fen long; the ring's circumference was five cun and four fen; both were carved and inlaid throughout.
translations.idiomatic: The hook was seven cun and three fen long, the ring's circumference was five cun and four fen, and both were carved and inlaid throughout.

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝永興二年四月，光祿勳府吏舍，夜壁下有青氣，得玉鉤、玦各一。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yongxing of Emperor Huan of Han, at the clerks' quarters of the Household of the Minister of the Imperial Household, at night there was azure vapor beneath the wall, and one jade hook and one jade ring were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Yongxing under Emperor Huan of Han, at the clerks' quarters of the Household of the Minister of the Imperial Household, azure vapor appeared beneath the wall at night, and one jade hook and one jade ring were found.

sentences.zh: 鉤長七寸三分，玦周五寸四分，身中皆雕鏤。

translations.literal: The hook was seven cun and three fen long; the ring's circumference was five cun and four fen; both were carved and inlaid throughout.
translations.idiomatic: The hook was seven cun and three fen long, the ring's circumference was five cun and four fen, and both were carved and inlaid throughout.

sentences.zh: 晉懷帝永嘉六年二月壬子，玉龜出灞水。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the second month of the sixth year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai of Jin, a jade tortoise emerged from the Ba River.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the second month of the sixth year of Yongjia under Emperor Huai of Jin, a jade tortoise emerged from the Ba River.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建興二年十月，大將軍劉琨掘地得玉璽，使參軍郎碩奉之歸于京師。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Jianxing of Emperor Min of Jin, the Grand General Liu Kun dug in the earth and obtained a jade seal; he sent the Staff Officer Lang Shuo to present it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Jianxing under Emperor Min of Jin, Grand General Liu Kun dug in the earth and obtained a jade seal; he sent Staff Officer Lang Shuo to present it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 建興二年十二月，涼州刺史張寔遣使獻行璽一紐，封送璽使關內侯。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Jianxing, Zhang Shi, Inspector of Liangzhou, sent an envoy to present one traveling seal with its cord; the envoy bearing the seal was enfeoffed as Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Jianxing, Zhang Shi, Inspector of Liangzhou, sent an envoy to present one traveling seal with its cord, and the envoy bearing the seal was enfeoffed as Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建武元年三月己酉，丹陽江寧民虞由墾土得白麒麟璽一紐，文曰「長壽萬年」。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day of the third month of the first year of Jianwu of Emperor Min of Jin, Yu You, a commoner of Jiangning in Danyang, by tilling the soil obtained one white qilin seal with its cord; the inscription read "Long Life for Ten Thousand Years."
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the third month of the first year of Jianwu under Emperor Min of Jin, Yu You, a commoner of Jiangning in Danyang, obtained by tilling the soil one white qilin seal with its cord inscribed "Long Life for Ten Thousand Years."

sentences.zh: 獻晉王。

translations.literal: It was presented to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: It was presented to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康八年九月，廬江舂穀縣留珪夜見門內有光，取得玉鼎一枚，外圍四寸。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Xiankang of Emperor Cheng of Jin, Liu Gui of Chungu County in Lujiang at night saw light within his gate and obtained one jade cauldron; its outer circumference was four cun.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin, Liu Gui of Chungu County in Lujiang saw light within his gate at night and obtained one jade cauldron with an outer circumference of four cun.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史路永以獻。

translations.literal: Lu Yong, Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yong, Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 著作郎曹毗上玉鼎頌。

translations.literal: Cao Pi, Gentleman of the Secretariat, submitted a hymn in praise of the jade cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi, Gentleman of the Secretariat, submitted a hymn in praise of the jade cauldron.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙十二年六月，左衞兵陳陽於東府前淮水中得玉璽一枚。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin, Chen Yang of the Left Guard Army obtained one jade seal in the Huai River before the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twelfth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, Chen Yang of the Left Guard Army obtained one jade seal in the Huai River before the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武帝大明元年五月戊寅，江乘縣民朱伯地中得玉璧，徑五寸八分，以獻。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day of the fifth month of the first year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, Zhu Bo, a commoner of Jiangcheng County, obtained a jade bi from the ground; its diameter was five cun and eight fen, and he presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of the fifth month of the first year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, Zhu Bo, a commoner of Jiangcheng County, obtained a jade bi from the ground with a diameter of five cun and eight fen and presented it.

sentences.zh: 大明四年二月乙巳，徐州刺史劉道隆於汴水得白玉戟，以獻。

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the second month of the fourth year of Daming, Liu Daolong, Inspector of Xuzhou, obtained a white jade halberd in the Bian River and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the second month of the fourth year of Daming, Liu Daolong, Inspector of Xuzhou, obtained a white jade halberd in the Bian River and presented it.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始五年十月庚辰，郢州獲玄璧，廣八寸五分，安西將軍蔡興宗以獻。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day of the tenth month of the fifth year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, a dark jade bi was obtained in Yingzhou; it was eight cun and five fen wide; Cai Xingzong, General Who Pacifies the West, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day of the tenth month of the fifth year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, a dark jade bi was obtained in Yingzhou, eight cun and five fen wide; Cai Xingzong, General Who Pacifies the West, presented it.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽四年十一月乙巳，吳興烏程余山道人慧獲蒼玉璧，太守蕭惠開以獻。

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yuanhui of the Deposed Emperor of Later Song, the Daoist Hui of Yushan in Wuxing, Wucheng, obtained a gray jade bi; the Prefect Xiao Hui Kai presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor of Later Song, the Daoist Hui of Yushan in Wucheng, Wuxing, obtained a gray jade bi, and Xiao Hui Kai, the Prefect, presented it.

sentences.zh: 金勝

translations.literal: Golden Sheng
translations.idiomatic: Golden Sheng

sentences.zh: 金勝，國平盜賊，四夷賓服則出。

translations.literal: The golden sheng—when the realm is at peace, bandits and robbers are subdued, and the four barbarians submit as guests, it emerges.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm is at peace, bandits and robbers are subdued, and the four barbarians submit as guests, the golden sheng appears.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和元年二月，舂穀民得金勝一枚，長五寸，狀如織勝。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yonghe of Emperor Mu of Jin, a commoner of Chungu obtained one golden sheng; it was five cun long and shaped like a woven sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu of Jin, a commoner of Chungu obtained one golden sheng five cun long, shaped like a woven sheng.

sentences.zh: 明年，桓溫平蜀。

translations.literal: The next year, Huan Wen pacified Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Huan Wen pacified Shu.

sentences.zh: 永和元年三月，廬江太守路永上言，於舂穀城北，見水岸邊有紫赤光，取得金狀如印，遣主簿李邁表送。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Yonghe, Lu Yong, Prefect of Lujiang, reported that north of Chungu city, on the water's bank, he saw purple-red light and obtained gold shaped like a seal; he sent his Chief Clerk Li Mai to present it in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Yonghe, Lu Yong, Prefect of Lujiang, reported that north of Chungu city he saw purple-red light on the water's bank, obtained gold shaped like a seal, and sent his Chief Clerk Li Mai to present it in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 吳孫晧天璽元年，吳郡言掘地得銀一，長尺，廣三分，刻上有年月字。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi of Sun Hao of Wu, Wu Commandery reported that by digging in the earth they obtained one piece of silver one chi long and three fen wide, with characters of year and month carved on it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi under Sun Hao of Wu, Wu Commandery reported that by digging in the earth they obtained one piece of silver one chi long and three fen wide, with characters of year and month carved upon it.

sentences.zh: 丹甑

translations.literal: Red Cauldron
translations.idiomatic: Red Cauldron

sentences.zh: 丹甑，五穀豐熟則出。

translations.literal: The red cauldron—when the five grains are abundantly ripe, it emerges.
translations.idiomatic: When the five grains are abundantly ripe, the red cauldron appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 白魚

translations.literal: White Fish
translations.idiomatic: White Fish

sentences.zh: 白魚，武王度孟津，中流入于王舟。

translations.literal: The white fish—when King Wu crossed Mengjin, midway in the flow it entered the king's boat.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu crossed the Mengjin ford, a white fish midway in the current entered the royal boat.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝泰始二年十月己巳，幸華林天淵池，白魚躍入御舟。

translations.literal: On the jisi day of the tenth month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, he visited the Celestial Abyss Pool in Hualin Park; a white fish leaped into the imperial boat.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the tenth month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, the emperor visited the Celestial Abyss Pool in Hualin Park, and a white fish leaped into the imperial boat.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和三年正月，車駕北巡，以太牢具祠北岳，有神魚躍出十數。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Yuanhe of Emperor Zhang of Han, the imperial carriage toured north; with the grand offering he sacrificed to the Northern Peak, and more than ten divine fish leaped out.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Yuanhe under Emperor Zhang of Han, the emperor toured north and, with the grand offering, sacrificed to the Northern Peak; more than ten divine fish leaped out.

sentences.zh: 金人

translations.literal: Golden Man
translations.idiomatic: Golden Man

sentences.zh: 金人，王者有盛德則游後池。

translations.literal: The golden man—when a king possesses abundant virtue, it roams the rear pool.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler possesses abundant virtue, the golden man roams the rear pool.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 木連理

translations.literal: Connected Trees
translations.idiomatic: Connected Trees

sentences.zh: 木連理，王者德澤純洽，八方合為一，則生。

translations.literal: Connected trees—when a king's virtue and grace are pure and harmonious, and the eight directions unite as one, they emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler's virtue and grace are pure and harmonious and the eight directions unite as one, connected trees emerge.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和中，木連理生郡國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, connected trees grew in commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era under Emperor Zhang of Han, connected trees appeared in commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 安帝元初三年正月丁丑，東平陵樹連理。

translations.literal: On the dingchou day of the first month of the third year of Yuanchu of Emperor An, trees at Dongping Mausoleum intertwined.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day of the first month of the third year of Yuanchu under Emperor An, trees at Dongping Mausoleum intertwined.

sentences.zh: 漢安帝延光三年七月，左馮翊衙有木連理。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Yanguang of Emperor An of Han, there were connected trees at the yamen of Left Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year of Yanguang under Emperor An of Han, connected trees appeared at the yamen of Left Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 延光三年七月，潁川定陵有木連理。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Yanguang, there were connected trees at Ding Mausoleum in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year of Yanguang, connected trees appeared at Ding Mausoleum in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝建和二年七月，河東有木連理。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Jianhe of Emperor Huan of Han, there were connected trees in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Jianhe under Emperor Huan of Han, connected trees appeared in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權黃武四年六月，皖口言有木連理。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Huangwu of Sun Quan of Wu, Wankou reported connected trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Huangwu under Sun Quan of Wu, Wankou reported connected trees.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初初，郡國二言木連理。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangchu of Emperor Wen of Wei, two commanderies and kingdoms reported connected trees.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, two commanderies and kingdoms reported connected trees.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始元年十二月，木連理生遼東力城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, connected trees grew at Licheng in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, connected trees appeared at Licheng in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年八月，木連理生河南成臯。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi, connected trees grew at Chenggao in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi, connected trees appeared at Chenggao in Henan.

sentences.zh: 泰始八年正月，木連理生東平范。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year of Taishi, connected trees grew at Fan in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year of Taishi, connected trees appeared at Fan in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 泰始八年五月甲辰，木連理生東平壽張。

translations.literal: On the jiachen day of the fifth month of the eighth year of Taishi, connected trees grew at Shouzhang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the fifth month of the eighth year of Taishi, connected trees appeared at Shouzhang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 泰始八年十月，木連理生建寧。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year of Taishi, connected trees grew in Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eighth year of Taishi, connected trees appeared in Jianning.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧元年正月，木連理生汝陰南頓。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xianning of Emperor Wu of Jin, connected trees grew at Nandun in Yingyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Xianning under Emperor Wu of Jin, connected trees appeared at Nandun in Yingyin.

sentences.zh: 咸寧二年四月，木連理生清河靈。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Xianning, connected trees grew at Ling in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Xianning, connected trees appeared at Ling in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 咸寧二年六月，木連理生燕國。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Xianning, connected trees grew in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Xianning, connected trees appeared in Yan.

sentences.zh: 咸寧三年七月壬辰，木連理生始平鄠。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the seventh month of the third year of Xianning, connected trees grew at E in Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the seventh month of the third year of Xianning, connected trees appeared at E in Shiping.

sentences.zh: 咸寧四年八月，木連理生陳留長垣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Xianning, connected trees grew at Changyuan in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Xianning, connected trees appeared at Changyuan in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 咸寧五年，木連理生義陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianning, connected trees grew in Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianning, connected trees appeared in Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 咸寧五年，木連理生樂安臨濟。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianning, connected trees grew at Linji in Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianning, connected trees appeared at Linji in Le'an.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康元年正月，木連理生涪陵永平。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, connected trees grew at Yongping in Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, connected trees appeared at Yongping in Fuling.

sentences.zh: 太康元年四月，木連理生頓丘。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Taikang, connected trees grew in Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Taikang, connected trees appeared in Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 太康元年五月，木連理二生濟陰乘氏，沛國。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Taikang, two connected trees grew in Chengshi, Jiyin, and in Pei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Taikang, two connected trees appeared in Chengshi, Jiyin, and in Pei.

sentences.zh: 太康元年七月，木連理生馮翊粟邑。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Taikang, connected trees grew at Suyi in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Taikang, connected trees appeared at Suyi in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 太康二年正月，木連理生滎陽密。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Taikang, connected trees grew at Mi in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Taikang, connected trees appeared at Mi in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 太康二年十月，木連理十三生南安羱道。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Taikang, thirteen connected trees grew at Yangdao in Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Taikang, thirteen connected trees appeared at Yangdao in Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 太康三年四月，木連理生琅邪華。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Taikang, connected trees grew at Hua in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Taikang, connected trees appeared at Hua in Langye.

sentences.zh: 太康三年六月，木連理生廣陵海西。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Taikang, connected trees grew at Haixi in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Taikang, connected trees appeared at Haixi in Guangling.

sentences.zh: 太康四年正月，木連理生馮翊臨晉，蜀郡成都。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Taikang, connected trees grew at Linjin in Fengyi and in Chengdu, Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year of Taikang, connected trees appeared at Linjin in Fengyi and in Chengdu, Shu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 太康四年十二月，木連理生扶風。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Taikang, connected trees grew in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Taikang, connected trees appeared in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 太康七年三月，木連理生河南新安。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year of Taikang, connected trees grew at Xin'an in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year of Taikang, connected trees appeared at Xin'an in Henan.

sentences.zh: 太康七年六月，木連理生始興中宿，南鄉筑陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Taikang, connected trees grew at Zhongsu in Shixing and at Zhuyang in Nanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Taikang, connected trees appeared at Zhongsu in Shixing and at Zhuyang in Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 太康八年四月，木連理生廬陵東昌。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Taikang, connected trees grew at Dongchang in Luling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Taikang, connected trees appeared at Dongchang in Luling.

sentences.zh: 太康八年九月，木連理生東萊盧鄉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Taikang, connected trees grew at Luxiang in Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Taikang, connected trees appeared at Luxiang in Donglai.

sentences.zh: 太康九年九月，木連理生陳留浚儀。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the ninth year of Taikang, connected trees grew at Junyi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the ninth year of Taikang, connected trees appeared at Junyi in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 太康十年十一月，木連理生鄱陽鄡陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the tenth year of Taikang, connected trees grew at Ziyang in Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the tenth year of Taikang, connected trees appeared at Ziyang in Poyang.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太熙元年二月，木連理生河南梁。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Taixi of Emperor Wu of Jin, connected trees grew at Liang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Taixi under Emperor Wu of Jin, connected trees appeared at Liang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康元年五月，木連理三生成都臨邛。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, three connected trees grew at Linqiong in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, three connected trees appeared at Linqiong in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 元康元年七月辛丑，梁國內史任式上言，武平界有柞櫟二樹，合為一體，連理。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day of the seventh month of the first year of Yuankang, Ren Shi, Administrator of Liang, reported that at the border of Wuping there were two trees, oak and cork oak, that merged into one body with intertwined branches.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the seventh month of the first year of Yuankang, Ren Shi, Administrator of Liang, reported that at the border of Wuping two trees, an oak and a cork oak, had merged into one body with intertwined branches.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建興二年三月庚辰，木連理生朱提。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day of the third month of the second year of Jianxing of Emperor Min of Jin, connected trees grew in Zhuti.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day of the third month of the second year of Jianxing under Emperor Min of Jin, connected trees appeared in Zhuti.

sentences.zh: 建興二年三月，木連理二生益州雙栢。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Jianxing, two connected trees grew at Shuangbai in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Jianxing, two connected trees appeared at Shuangbai in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 建興二年六月，木連理生襄平。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Jianxing, connected trees grew in Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Jianxing, connected trees appeared in Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建武元年閏月乙丑，木連理生嵩山。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the intercalary month of the first year of Jianwu of Emperor Min of Jin, connected trees grew on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the intercalary month of the first year of Jianwu under Emperor Min of Jin, connected trees appeared on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 建武元年八月甲午，木連理生汝陰。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day of the eighth month of the first year of Jianwu, connected trees grew in Yingyin.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the eighth month of the first year of Jianwu, connected trees appeared in Yingyin.

sentences.zh: 建武元年十一月，木連理生武昌，大將軍王敦以聞晉王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Jianwu, connected trees grew in Wuchang; Grand General Wang Dun reported it to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Jianwu, connected trees appeared in Wuchang, and Grand General Wang Dun reported it to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 建武元年十一月癸酉，木連理生汝陰，太守以聞。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day of the eleventh month of the first year of Jianwu, connected trees grew in Yingyin; the prefect reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the eleventh month of the first year of Jianwu, connected trees appeared in Yingyin, and the prefect reported it.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興元年七月戊辰，木連理生武昌，大將軍王敦以聞。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the seventh month of the first year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin, connected trees grew in Wuchang; Grand General Wang Dun reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the seventh month of the first year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin, connected trees appeared in Wuchang, and Grand General Wang Dun reported it.

sentences.zh: 太興三年十一月，木連理生零陵永昌。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Taixing, connected trees grew at Yongchang in Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Taixing, connected trees appeared at Yongchang in Lingling.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和八年五月己巳，木連理生昌黎咸和。

translations.literal: On the jisi day of the fifth month of the eighth year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin, connected trees grew at Xianhe in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the fifth month of the eighth year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng of Jin, connected trees appeared at Xianhe in Changli.

sentences.zh: 咸康三年三月庚戌，木連理生平州世子府治故園中。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day of the third month of the third year of Xiankang, connected trees grew in the former garden of the Heir Apparent's residence at Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the third month of the third year of Xiankang, connected trees appeared in the former garden of the Heir Apparent's residence at Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸康七年十二月，吳國內史王恬上言，木連理生吳縣沙里。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Xiankang, Wang Tian, Administrator of Wu, reported that connected trees grew at Shali in Wuxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Xiankang, Wang Tian, Administrator of Wu, reported that connected trees appeared at Shali in Wuxian.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和五年二月癸丑，臨海太守藍田侯述言郡界木連理。

translations.literal: On the guichou day of the second month of the fifth year of Yonghe of Emperor Mu of Jin, Hou Shu, Prefect of Linhai and Marquis of Lantian, reported connected trees within his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day of the second month of the fifth year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu of Jin, Hou Shu, Prefect of Linhai and Marquis of Lantian, reported connected trees within his commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝寧康三年六月辛卯，江寧縣建興里僑民留康家樹，異本連理。

translations.literal: On the xinmao day of the sixth month of the third year of Ningkang of Emperor Xiao of Jin, trees at the home of Liu Kang, a settler of Jianxing Lane in Jiangning County, of different species had intertwined branches.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the sixth month of the third year of Ningkang under Emperor Xiao of Jin, trees at the home of Liu Kang, a settler of Jianxing Lane in Jiangning County, of different species had intertwined branches.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元十一年四月壬申，琅邪費有榆木，異根連理，相去四尺九寸。

translations.literal: On the renshen day of the fourth month of the eleventh year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiao of Jin, in Fei, Langye, there was an elm tree with separate roots but intertwined branches, four cun and nine fen apart.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day of the fourth month of the eleventh year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiao of Jin, in Fei, Langye, an elm tree with separate roots had intertwined branches four cun and nine fen apart.

sentences.zh: 太元十八年十月戊午，臨川東興令惠欣之言，縣東南溪傍有白銀樹、芳靈樹、李樹，並連理。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day of the tenth month of the eighteenth year of Taiyuan, Huixin, Magistrate of Dongxing in Linchuan, reported that southeast of the county by a stream there were silver-leaf, fragrant-spirit, and plum trees, all with intertwined branches.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the tenth month of the eighteenth year of Taiyuan, Huixin, Magistrate of Dongxing in Linchuan, reported that southeast of the county by a stream there were silver-leaf, fragrant-spirit, and plum trees, all with intertwined branches.
