translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of the second month of the seventh year of Taishi, connected trees appeared at Qiantang in Wu Commandery, and Wang Yanzhi, grand administrator, reported it.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，木連理生豫州界內，刺史劉懷珍以聞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming, connected trees grew within the borders of Yuzhou; Liu Huaizhen, provincial inspector, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming, connected trees appeared within the borders of Yuzhou, and Liu Huaizhen, provincial inspector, reported it.

sentences.zh: 比目魚

translations.literal: Flatfish
translations.idiomatic: Flatfish

sentences.zh: 比目魚，王者德及幽隱則見。

translations.literal: Flatfish—when a king's virtue reaches even the hidden and obscure, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler's virtue reaches even the hidden and obscure, flatfish appear.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 珊瑚鉤

translations.literal: Coral Hook
translations.idiomatic: Coral Hook

sentences.zh: 珊瑚鉤，王者恭信則見。

translations.literal: Coral hook—when a king is reverent and trustworthy, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler is reverent and trustworthy, the coral hook appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 芝草

translations.literal: Spirit Mushroom
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Mushroom

sentences.zh: 芝草，王者慈仁則生。

translations.literal: Spirit mushroom—when a king is compassionate and benevolent, it grows.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler is compassionate and benevolent, spirit mushrooms grow.

sentences.zh: 食之令人度世。

translations.literal: Eating it enables one to transcend the worldly realm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who eat it are said to transcend the mortal world.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝元封二年，甘泉宮內產芝，九莖連葉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng of Emperor Wu of Han, spirit mushrooms grew within Ganquan Palace—nine stalks with connected leaves.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Wu of Han, spirit mushrooms appeared within Ganquan Palace: nine stalks with connected leaves.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝元康四年，金芝九莖，產于函德殿銅池中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuankang of Emperor Xuan of Han, golden spirit mushrooms with nine stalks grew in the bronze pool of Hande Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuankang under Emperor Xuan of Han, golden spirit mushrooms with nine stalks appeared in the bronze pool of Hande Hall.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝永平十七年春，芝生前殿。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year of Yongping of Emperor Ming of Han, spirit mushrooms grew before the front hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year of Yongping under Emperor Ming of Han, spirit mushrooms appeared before the front hall.

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝建和元年四月，芝草生中黃藏府。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Jianhe of Emperor Huan of Han, spirit mushrooms grew in the Central Yellow Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Jianhe under Emperor Huan of Han, spirit mushrooms appeared in the Central Yellow Treasury.

sentences.zh: 宋從帝昇明二年，宣城山中生紫芝一株，在所獲以獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming of Emperor Shun of Song, one stalk of purple spirit mushroom grew in the mountains of Xuancheng; those at the site captured it and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming under Emperor Shun of Song, a single stalk of purple spirit mushroom grew in the mountains of Xuancheng, and those at the site captured it and presented it.

sentences.zh: 明月珠，王者不盡介鱗之物則出。

translations.literal: Bright Moon Pearl—when a king does not exhaust creatures with shells and scales, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler does not exhaust creatures with shells and scales, the Bright Moon Pearl appears.

sentences.zh: 漢高后景帝時，會稽人朱仲獻三寸四寸珠。

translations.literal: During the reigns of Empress Gao and Emperor Jing of Han, Zhu Zhong of Kuaiji presented pearls measuring three and four cun.
translations.idiomatic: During the reigns of Empress Gao and Emperor Jing of Han, Zhu Zhong of Kuaiji presented pearls measuring three and four cun.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和中，郡國獻明珠。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, commanderies and kingdoms presented luminous pearls.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign of Emperor Zhang of Han, commanderies and kingdoms presented luminous pearls.

sentences.zh: 巨鬯，三禺之禾，一稃二米，王者宗廟修則出。

translations.literal: Great Libation: grain from Mount Sanyu, one husk and two grains—when a king's ancestral temple is maintained, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: Great Libation is grain from Mount Sanyu, one husk bearing two grains; when a ruler maintains the ancestral temple, it appears.

sentences.zh: 黃帝時，南夷乘白鹿來獻鬯。

translations.literal: In the time of the Yellow Emperor, the southern Yi came riding white deer to present libation grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of the Yellow Emperor, the southern Yi came riding white deer to present libation grain.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和中，秬秠生郡國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, black and red sacrificial millet grew in commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign of Emperor Zhang of Han, black and red sacrificial millet appeared in commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 華平，其枝正平，王者有德則生。

translations.literal: Splendor Level—its branches are perfectly level; when a king has virtue, it grows.
translations.idiomatic: Splendor Level has perfectly level branches; when a ruler possesses virtue, it grows.

sentences.zh: 德剛則仰，德弱則低。

translations.literal: When virtue is strong, it rises; when virtue is weak, it lowers.
translations.idiomatic: When virtue is strong, it rises; when virtue is weak, it bows low.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和中，華平生郡國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, Splendor Level grew in commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign of Emperor Zhang of Han, Splendor Level appeared in commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 平露

translations.literal: Level Dew
translations.idiomatic: Level Dew

sentences.zh: 平露，如蓋，以察四方之政。

translations.literal: Level Dew, like a canopy, is used to inspect governance in the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Level Dew resembles a canopy and is used to inspect governance in the four directions.

sentences.zh: 其國不平，則隨方而傾。

translations.literal: If a state is not equitable, it tilts toward that direction.
translations.idiomatic: If a state's governance is not equitable, it tilts toward that direction.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 蓂莢

translations.literal: Ming Pod
translations.idiomatic: Ming Pod

sentences.zh: 蓂莢，一名歷莢，夾階而生，一日生一葉，從朔而生，望而止，十六日，日落一葉，若月小，則一葉萎而不落。

translations.literal: Ming pod, also called Calendar Pod, grows flanking the steps; one leaf grows each day, starting from the new moon and stopping at the full moon; from the sixteenth day, one leaf falls each day; if the month is short, one leaf withers but does not fall.
translations.idiomatic: The ming pod, also called the calendar pod, grows along the steps. One leaf appears each day from the new moon until the full moon; after the sixteenth, one leaf falls each day. In a short month, one leaf withers but does not fall.

sentences.zh: 堯時生階。

translations.literal: In the time of Yao, it grew on the steps.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Yao, it grew on the steps.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 萐甫

translations.literal: Shaifu
translations.idiomatic: Shaifu

sentences.zh: 萐甫，一名倚扇，狀如蓬，大枝葉小，根根如絲，轉而成風，殺蠅。

translations.literal: Shaifu, also called Leaning Fan, is shaped like fleabane, with large branches and small leaves; its roots are like threads; when spun it becomes wind and kills flies.
translations.idiomatic: Shaifu, also called Leaning Fan, resembles fleabane, with large branches and small leaves and threadlike roots; spun, it stirs wind that kills flies.

sentences.zh: 堯時生於廚。

translations.literal: In the time of Yao, it grew in the kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Yao, it grew in the kitchen.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 朱草

translations.literal: Vermilion Grass
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion Grass

sentences.zh: 朱草，草之精也，世有聖人之德則生。

translations.literal: Vermilion grass is the essence of grasses; when the age has the virtue of a sage, it grows.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion grass is the quintessence of grasses; when an age possesses the virtue of a sage, it grows.

sentences.zh: 漢光武建武中元元年五月，京師有赤草生水涯。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Zhongyuan of the Jianwu era of Emperor Guangwu of Han, red grass grew at the water's edge in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Zhongyuan in the Jianwu era under Emperor Guangwu of Han, red grass appeared at the water's edge in the capital.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和中，朱草生郡國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, vermilion grass grew in commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign of Emperor Zhang of Han, vermilion grass appeared in commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝初，朱草生文昌殿側。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reign of Emperor Wen of Wei, vermilion grass grew beside Wenchang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the reign of Emperor Wen of Wei, vermilion grass appeared beside Wenchang Hall.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十一年，朱草生蜀郡郫縣王之家，益州刺史甄法崇以聞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, vermilion grass grew at the Wang family's home in Pi County, Shu Commandery; Zhen Fachong, Inspector of Yizhou, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, vermilion grass appeared at the Wang family's home in Pi County in Shu Commandery, and Zhen Fachong, Inspector of Yizhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 景星

translations.literal: Luminous Star
translations.idiomatic: Luminous Star

sentences.zh: 景星，大星也。

translations.literal: Luminous Star is a great star.
translations.idiomatic: The Luminous Star is a great star.

sentences.zh: 狀如半月，於晦朔助月為明。

translations.literal: Shaped like a half moon, at the dark of the moon and the new moon it assists the moon as brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Shaped like a half moon, it augments the moon's light at the dark of the moon and at the new moon.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 賓連闊達

translations.literal: Binlian Kuoda
translations.idiomatic: Binlian Kuoda

sentences.zh: 賓連闊達，生於房室，王者御后妃有節則生。

translations.literal: Binlian Kuoda grows in the inner chambers; when a king governs his consorts with propriety, it grows.
translations.idiomatic: Binlian Kuoda grows in the inner chambers; when a ruler governs his consorts with propriety, it appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 渠搜

translations.literal: Qusou
translations.idiomatic: Qusou

sentences.zh: 渠搜，禹時來獻裘。

translations.literal: Qusou, in the time of Yu, came to present furs.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Yu, Qusou came to present furs.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 浪井

translations.literal: Surging Well
translations.idiomatic: Surging Well

sentences.zh: 浪井，不鑿自成，王者清靜則應。

translations.literal: Surging Well forms without drilling; when a king is pure and tranquil, it responds.
translations.idiomatic: The Surging Well forms without being drilled; when a ruler is pure and tranquil, it appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 西王母

translations.literal: Queen Mother of the West
translations.idiomatic: Queen Mother of the West

sentences.zh: 西王母，舜時來獻白環白琯。

translations.literal: Queen Mother of the West, in the time of Shun, came to present a white ring and white flute.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Shun, the Queen Mother of the West came to present a white ring and a white flute.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 越常

translations.literal: Yuechang
translations.idiomatic: Yuechang

sentences.zh: 越常，周公時來獻白雉、象牙。

translations.literal: Yuechang, in the time of the Duke of Zhou, came to present a white pheasant and ivory.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of the Duke of Zhou, Yuechang came to present a white pheasant and ivory.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 漢平帝元始元年正月，越常重譯獻白雉一，黑雉二，詔三公薦宗廟。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yuanshi of Emperor Ping of Han, Yuechang presented through repeated translation one white pheasant and two black pheasants; an edict ordered the Three Excellencies to recommend them for the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yuanshi under Emperor Ping of Han, Yuechang presented, through layers of translation, one white pheasant and two black pheasants; an edict ordered the Three Excellencies to recommend them for the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 漢光武建武十三年九月，南越獻白雉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Jianwu of Emperor Guangwu of Han, Southern Yue presented a white pheasant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Jianwu under Emperor Guangwu of Han, Southern Yue presented a white pheasant.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和中，白雉見郡國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, white pheasants appeared in commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign of Emperor Zhang of Han, white pheasants appeared in commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝永康元年十一月，白雉見西河。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yongkang of Emperor Huan of Han, a white pheasant appeared in Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yongkang under Emperor Huan of Han, a white pheasant appeared in Xihe.

sentences.zh: 漢獻帝延康元年四月丁巳，饒安縣言白雉見；

translations.literal: On the dingsi day of the fourth month of the first year of Yankang of Emperor Xian of Han, Rao'an County reported that a white pheasant had appeared;
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the fourth month of the first year of Yankang under Emperor Xian of Han, Rao'an County reported that a white pheasant had appeared;

sentences.zh: 又郡國十九言白雉見。

translations.literal: Nineteen commanderies and kingdoms also reported that white pheasants had appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen commanderies and kingdoms also reported white pheasant sightings.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧元年四月丁巳，白雉見安豐松滋。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day of the fourth month of the first year of Xianning of Emperor Wu of Jin, a white pheasant appeared at Songzi in Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the fourth month of the first year of Xianning under Emperor Wu of Jin, a white pheasant appeared at Songzi in Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 咸寧元年十二月丙午，白雉見梁國睢陽，梁王肜獲以獻。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day of the twelfth month of the first year of Xianning, a white pheasant appeared at Suiyang in Liang State; Rong, Prince of Liang, captured it and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day of the twelfth month of the first year of Xianning, a white pheasant appeared at Suiyang in Liang State, and Rong, Prince of Liang, captured it and presented it.

sentences.zh: 咸寧三年十一月，白雉見渤海饒安，相阮溫獲以獻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Xianning, a white pheasant appeared at Rao'an in Bohai; Chancellor Ruan Wen captured it and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Xianning, a white pheasant appeared at Rao'an in Bohai, and Chancellor Ruan Wen captured it and presented it.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康元年九月庚戌，白雉見中山。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day of the ninth month of the first year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, a white pheasant appeared in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the ninth month of the first year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, a white pheasant appeared in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建興三年十二月戊午，白雉見襄平。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day of the twelfth month of the third year of Jianxing of Emperor Min of Jin, a white pheasant appeared at Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the twelfth month of the third year of Jianxing under Emperor Min of Jin, a white pheasant appeared at Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 建興三年十二月戊午，白雉見。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day of the twelfth month of the third year of Jianxing, a white pheasant appeared.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the twelfth month of the third year of Jianxing, a white pheasant appeared.

sentences.zh: 安帝義熙七年五月，白雉見豫章南昌。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin, a white pheasant appeared at Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, a white pheasant appeared at Nanchang in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉五年五月庚辰，白雉見東莞莒縣，太守劉玄以聞。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, a white pheasant appeared at Ju County in Dongguan; Liu Xuan, grand administrator, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, a white pheasant appeared at Ju County in Dongguan, and Liu Xuan, grand administrator, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十六年二月，白雉見陳郡，豫州刺史長沙王義欣以獻。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year of Yuanjia, a white pheasant appeared in Chen Commandery; Yixin, Prince of Changsha and Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixteenth year of Yuanjia, a white pheasant appeared in Chen Commandery, and Yixin, Prince of Changsha and Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十八年二月癸亥，白雉見南汝陰宋縣，太守文道恩以獻。

translations.literal: On the guihai day of the second month of the eighteenth year of Yuanjia, a white pheasant appeared at Song County in South Ruyin; Wen Daoen, grand administrator, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day of the second month of the eighteenth year of Yuanjia, a white pheasant appeared at Song County in South Ruyin, and Wen Daoen, grand administrator, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年六月，白雉見高平方與縣，徐州刺史臧質以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, a white pheasant appeared at Fangyu County in Gaoping; Zang Zhi, Inspector of Xuzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twentieth year of Yuanjia, a white pheasant appeared at Fangyu County in Gaoping, and Zang Zhi, Inspector of Xuzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年三月戊寅，白雉見東安，沛郡各一，徐、兗二州刺史武陵王獲以獻。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day of the third month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, a white pheasant appeared in Dong'an and one in Pei Commandery; Liu Jun, Prince of Wuling and Inspector of Xuzhou and Yanzhou, captured them and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of the third month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, a white pheasant appeared in Dong'an and one in Pei Commandery, and Liu Jun, Prince of Wuling and Inspector of Xuzhou and Yanzhou, captured them and presented them.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明二年三月己巳，白雉雌雄各一見海陵，南兗州刺史竟陵王誕以獻。

translations.literal: On the jisi day of the third month of the second year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, one male and one female white pheasant appeared at Hailing; Dan, Prince of Jingling and Inspector of South Yanzhou, presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the third month of the second year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, one male and one female white pheasant appeared at Hailing, and Dan, Prince of Jingling and Inspector of South Yanzhou, presented them.

sentences.zh: 大明五年十二月，白雉見秦郡，南兗州刺史晉安王子勛以獻。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Daming, a white pheasant appeared in Qin Commandery; Zixun, Prince of Jin'an and Inspector of South Yanzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Daming, a white pheasant appeared in Qin Commandery, and Zixun, Prince of Jin'an and Inspector of South Yanzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 大明八年二月丁卯，白雉見南郡江陵，荊州刺史臨海王子頊以獻。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day of the second month of the eighth year of Daming, a white pheasant appeared at Jiangling in Nan Commandery; Zixiang, Prince of Linhai and Inspector of Jingzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day of the second month of the eighth year of Daming, a white pheasant appeared at Jiangling in Nan Commandery, and Zixiang, Prince of Linhai and Inspector of Jingzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝永光元年正月丙午，白雉見渤海，青州刺史王玄謨以獻。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day of the first month of the first year of Yongguang of the Former Deposed Emperor, a white pheasant appeared in Bohai; Wang Xuanmo, Inspector of Qingzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day of the first month of the first year of Yongguang under the Former Deposed Emperor, a white pheasant appeared in Bohai, and Wang Xuanmo, Inspector of Qingzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 永光元年三月甲午朔，白雉見新蔡，豫州刺史劉德願以獻。

translations.literal: On the jiawu new moon of the third month of the first year of Yongguang, a white pheasant appeared in Xincai; Liu Deyuan, Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu new moon of the third month of the first year of Yongguang, a white pheasant appeared in Xincai, and Liu Deyuan, Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 黃銀紫玉

translations.literal: Yellow Silver and Purple Jade
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Silver and Purple Jade

sentences.zh: 黃銀紫玉，王者不藏金玉，則黃銀紫玉光見深山。

translations.literal: Yellow silver and purple jade—when a king does not hoard gold and jade, the light of yellow silver and purple jade appears in deep mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler does not hoard gold and jade, the radiance of yellow silver and purple jade appears in deep mountains.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝泰始二年八月，於赭圻城南得紫玉一段，圍三尺二寸，長一尺，厚七尺。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, a section of purple jade was found south of Zhuge city: circumference three chi two cun, length one chi, thickness seven chi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, a section of purple jade was found south of Zhuge city, measuring three chi two cun in circumference, one chi in length, and seven chi in thickness.

sentences.zh: 太宗攻為二爵，以獻武、文二廟。

translations.literal: The Taizong had it worked into two libation cups and presented them to the temples of Emperor Wu and Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had it carved into two libation cups and presented them to the temples of Emperor Wu and Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 玉女

translations.literal: Jade Maiden
translations.idiomatic: Jade Maiden

sentences.zh: 玉女，天賜妾也。

translations.literal: The jade maiden is a consort granted by Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Maiden is a consort granted by Heaven.

sentences.zh: 禮含文嘉曰：「禹卑宮室，盡力溝洫，百穀用成，神龍女降。」

translations.literal: The Rites: Hanwen Jia says: "Yu kept his palace humble, exerted himself in ditches and canals, the hundred grains were brought to completion, and the divine dragon maiden descended."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites: Hanwen Jia says, "Yu kept his palace humble and labored at ditches and canals until the hundred grains flourished; then the divine dragon maiden descended."

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 地珠

translations.literal: Earth Pearl
translations.idiomatic: Earth Pearl

sentences.zh: 地珠，王者不以財為寶則生珠。

translations.literal: Earth pearl—when a king does not treat wealth as treasure, pearls are produced.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler does not treat wealth as treasure, earth pearls appear.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 天鹿

translations.literal: Celestial Deer
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Deer

sentences.zh: 天鹿者，純靈之獸也。

translations.literal: The celestial deer is a beast of pure spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Deer is a beast of pure spirit.

sentences.zh: 五色光耀洞明，王者道備則至。

translations.literal: Its five colors shine brilliantly and penetrate with clarity; when a king's Way is complete, it arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Its five colors blaze with penetrating brilliance; when a ruler's Way is complete, it appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 甪端

translations.literal: Luduan
translations.idiomatic: Luduan

sentences.zh: 甪端者，日行萬八千里，又曉四夷之語，明君聖主在位，明達方外幽遠之事，則奉書而至。

translations.literal: Luduan travels eighteen thousand li in a day and understands the languages of the four barbarian peoples. When a wise and sage sovereign occupies the throne and comprehends affairs beyond the borders and in distant lands, it comes bearing documents.
translations.idiomatic: Luduan travels eighteen thousand li in a day and understands the languages of the four quarters. When a wise and sage sovereign sits the throne and comprehends distant and hidden affairs beyond the realm, it arrives bearing written messages.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 周印

translations.literal: Zhou Seal
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Seal

sentences.zh: 周印者，神獸之名也，星宿之變化。

translations.literal: Zhou Seal is the name of a divine beast, [embodying] the transformations of the stars and constellations.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Seal is the name of a divine beast associated with the transformations of the stars and constellations.

sentences.zh: 王者德盛則至。

translations.literal: When a king's virtue is abundant, it arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler's virtue is abundant, it appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 飛菟

translations.literal: Flying Hare
translations.idiomatic: Flying Hare

sentences.zh: 飛菟者，神馬之名也，日行三萬里。

translations.literal: Flying Hare is the name of a divine horse; it travels thirty thousand li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: The Flying Hare is a divine horse that travels thirty thousand li in a day.

sentences.zh: 禹治水勤勞歷年，救民之害，天應其德而至。

translations.literal: Yu labored year after year at controlling the waters, rescuing the people from disaster; Heaven responded to his virtue and it arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yu toiled for years to control the waters and rescue the people from disaster; Heaven responded to his virtue, and the Flying Hare appeared.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 澤獸

translations.literal: Marsh Beast
translations.idiomatic: Marsh Beast

sentences.zh: 澤獸，黃帝時巡狩至於東濱，澤獸出，能言，達知萬物之精，以戒於民，為時除害。

translations.literal: The marsh beast: when the Yellow Emperor on tour reached the eastern shore, the marsh beast emerged; it could speak and thoroughly knew the essences of the ten thousand things; it admonished the people and removed harms for the age.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Emperor on tour reached the eastern shore, the Marsh Beast emerged. It could speak and knew the essences of all things; it warned the people and removed the age's disasters.

sentences.zh: 賢君明德幽遠則來。

translations.literal: When a worthy ruler's bright virtue reaches into the hidden and distant, it comes.
translations.idiomatic: When a worthy ruler's bright virtue reaches into hidden and distant places, it appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 𪊸者

translations.literal: Bozhe
translations.idiomatic: Bozhe

sentences.zh: 𪊸者，幽隱之獸也，有明王在位則來，為時辟除災害。

translations.literal: Bozhe is a beast of hidden places; when a bright king occupies the throne, it comes and removes disasters for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhe is a beast of hidden places. When a bright king sits the throne, it appears and dispels the age's disasters.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 騕[䮍-灬]

translations.literal: Yaoshuang
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshuang

sentences.zh: 騕[䮍-灬]者，神馬也，與飛菟同，亦各隨其方而至，以明君德也。

translations.literal: Yaoshuang is a divine horse; like the Flying Hare, it also arrives from each direction according to its quarter, to manifest a ruler's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshuang is a divine horse. Like the Flying Hare, it appears from each direction in turn, manifesting a ruler's virtue.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 同心鳥

translations.literal: Concentric Bird
translations.idiomatic: Concentric Bird

sentences.zh: 同心鳥，王者德及遐方，四夷合同則至。

translations.literal: Concentric bird—when a king's virtue reaches distant regions and the four barbarians unite in harmony, it arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler's virtue reaches distant lands and the four quarters unite in harmony, the Concentric Bird appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 趹蹄

translations.literal: Jueti
translations.idiomatic: Jueti

sentences.zh: 趹蹄者，后土之獸，自能言語。

translations.literal: Jueti is a beast of Queen Earth and can speak of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Jueti is a beast of Queen Earth and can speak on its own.

sentences.zh: 王者仁孝於國則來。

translations.literal: When a king is filial and benevolent toward the state, it comes.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler is filial and benevolent toward the realm, it appears.

sentences.zh: 禹治水而至。

translations.literal: It arrived when Yu controlled the waters.
translations.idiomatic: It appeared when Yu controlled the waters.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 紫達

translations.literal: Zida
translations.idiomatic: Zida

sentences.zh: 紫達，王者仁義行則見。

translations.literal: Zida—when a king practices benevolence and righteousness, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler practices benevolence and righteousness, Zida appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 小鳥生大鳥

translations.literal: Small Birds Giving Birth to Great Birds
translations.idiomatic: Small Birds Giving Birth to Great Birds

sentences.zh: 小鳥生大鳥，王者土地開闢則至。

translations.literal: Small birds giving birth to great birds—when a king opens and settles the land, it arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler opens and settles the land, small birds giving birth to great birds appear.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 河精

translations.literal: River Essence
translations.idiomatic: River Essence

sentences.zh: 河精者，人頭魚身，師曠時所受讖也。

translations.literal: The river essence has a human head and fish body; it was the prophecy received in the time of Shi Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: The River Essence has a human head and fish body; it was the prophecy Shi Kuang received in his age.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 延嬉

translations.literal: Yanxi
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi

sentences.zh: 延嬉，王者孝道行則至。

translations.literal: Yanxi—when a king practices filial piety, it arrives.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler practices filial piety, Yanxi appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 大貝

translations.literal: Great Shell
translations.idiomatic: Great Shell

sentences.zh: 大貝，王者不貪財寶則出。

translations.literal: Great shell—when a king does not covet treasure, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler does not covet treasure, the Great Shell appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 威蕤

translations.literal: Weirui
translations.idiomatic: Weirui

sentences.zh: 威蕤，王者禮備則生於殿前。

translations.literal: Weirui—when a king's rites are complete, it grows before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler's rites are complete, Weirui grows before the palace hall.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 醴泉

translations.literal: Sweet Spring
translations.idiomatic: Sweet Spring

sentences.zh: 醴泉，水之精也，甘美。

translations.literal: Sweet spring is the essence of water and is sweet and fine.
translations.idiomatic: The Sweet Spring is the quintessence of water, sweet and pure.

sentences.zh: 王者修理則出。

translations.literal: When a king governs well, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler governs well, it appears.

sentences.zh: 漢光武建武中元元年五月，醴泉出京師及郡國。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Zhongyuan of the Jianwu era of Emperor Guangwu of Han, sweet springs appeared in the capital and in commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Zhongyuan in the Jianwu era under Emperor Guangwu of Han, sweet springs appeared in the capital and in commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 飲醴泉者，痼病皆愈；

translations.literal: Those who drank the sweet spring—all chronic ailments were cured;
translations.idiomatic: Those who drank from the Sweet Spring found all chronic ailments cured;

sentences.zh: 獨眇者蹇者不差。

translations.literal: only the blind and the lame were not improved.
translations.idiomatic: only the blind and the lame were not healed.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝初，邵國二言醴泉出。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reign of Emperor Wen of Wei, two commanderies and kingdoms reported that sweet springs had appeared.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the reign of Emperor Wen of Wei, two commanderies and kingdoms reported that sweet springs had appeared.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十二年，衡陽湘鄉醴泉出縣庭，荊州刺史臨川王義慶以聞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, a sweet spring appeared in the county courtyard at Xiangxiang in Hengyang; Yiqing, Prince of Linchuan and Inspector of Jingzhou, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, a sweet spring appeared in the county courtyard at Xiangxiang in Hengyang, and Yiqing, Prince of Linchuan and Inspector of Jingzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝孝建三年九月甲戌，細仗隊省井泉春夏深不盈尺，忽至一丈，有五色，水清澄，醴味，汲引不窮。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day of the ninth month of the third year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiao of Song, the well spring at the Ceremonial Guard Detachment quarters was in summer and spring no more than a foot deep, but suddenly rose to one zhang; it had five colors, clear water, a sweet taste, and drawing from it was inexhaustible.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day of the ninth month of the third year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiao of Song, the well at the Ceremonial Guard Detachment quarters was usually less than a foot deep in spring and summer, but suddenly rose to ten feet. Its water was five-colored, clear, and sweet, and the supply seemed inexhaustible.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明二年三月壬子，北汝陰樓煩平地出醴泉，豫州刺史宗慤以聞。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the third month of the second year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, a sweet spring appeared on level ground at Loufan in North Ruyin; Zong Que, Inspector of Yuzhou, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the third month of the second year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, a sweet spring appeared on level ground at Loufan in North Ruyin, and Zong Que, Inspector of Yuzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰豫元年四月乙酉，會稽山陰思義醴泉出，太守蔡興宗以聞。

translations.literal: On the yiyou day of the fourth month of the first year of Taiyu of Emperor Ming of Song, a sweet spring appeared at Siyi in Shanyin, Kuaiji; Cai Xingzong, grand administrator, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the fourth month of the first year of Taiyu under Emperor Ming of Song, a sweet spring appeared at Siyi in Shanyin, Kuaiji, and Cai Xingzong, grand administrator, reported it.

sentences.zh: 日月揚光

translations.literal: Sun and Moon Radiating Light
translations.idiomatic: Sun and Moon Radiating Light

sentences.zh: 日月揚光，日者，人君象也，人君不假臣下之權，則日月揚光明。

translations.literal: Sun and moon radiating light—the sun is the image of the ruler; when the ruler does not delegate power to his ministers, the sun and moon radiate brightness.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is the image of the ruler. When a ruler does not delegate authority to his ministers, the sun and moon blaze with light.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 芝英

translations.literal: Spirit Bloom
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Bloom

sentences.zh: 芝英者，王者親近耆老，養有道，則生。

translations.literal: Spirit bloom—when a king draws near to the aged and nourishes those who possess the Way, it grows.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler draws near to the aged and nourishes those who possess the Way, spirit bloom appears.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和中，芝英生郡國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, spirit bloom grew in commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign of Emperor Zhang of Han, spirit bloom appeared in commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 碧石

translations.literal: Jade-green Stone
translations.idiomatic: Jade-green Stone

sentences.zh: 碧石者，玩好之物棄則至。

translations.literal: Jade-green stone—when objects of play and pleasure are cast aside, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: When objects of play and pleasure are cast aside, jade-green stone appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 玉罋

translations.literal: Jade Jar
translations.idiomatic: Jade Jar

sentences.zh: 玉罋者，不汲而滿，王者清廉則出。

translations.literal: Jade jar—it fills without being drawn from; when a king is pure and incorrupt, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Jar fills without being drawn from; when a ruler is pure and incorrupt, it appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 山車

translations.literal: Mountain Cart
translations.idiomatic: Mountain Cart

sentences.zh: 山車者，山藏之精也。

translations.literal: Mountain cart is the essence of mountain stores.
translations.idiomatic: The Mountain Cart is the quintessence of what the mountains hold.

sentences.zh: 不藏金玉，山澤以時，通山海之饒，以給天下，則山成其車。

translations.literal: When gold and jade are not hoarded, mountains and marshes are used in season, and the bounty of mountains and seas is brought forth to supply the realm, then the mountains form themselves into a cart.
translations.idiomatic: When gold and jade are not hoarded, mountains and marshes are used in season, and the bounty of mountains and seas is brought forth to supply the realm, the mountains themselves take the form of a cart.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 雞駭犀

translations.literal: Startled Chicken Rhinoceros
translations.idiomatic: Startled Chicken Rhinoceros

sentences.zh: 雞駭犀，王者賤難得之物則出。

translations.literal: Startled chicken rhinoceros—when a king holds cheap what is hard to obtain, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler holds cheap what is hard to obtain, the Startled Chicken Rhinoceros appears.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 陵出黑丹

translations.literal: Black Cinnabar Emanating from Tombs
translations.idiomatic: Black Cinnabar Emanating from Tombs

sentences.zh: 陵出黑丹，王者修至孝則出。

translations.literal: Black cinnabar emanating from tombs—when a king cultivates utmost filial piety, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler cultivates utmost filial piety, black cinnabar emanates from tombs.

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing in source)

sentences.zh: 神鼎

translations.literal: Divine Cauldron
translations.idiomatic: Divine Cauldron

sentences.zh: 神鼎者，質文之精也。

translations.literal: The divine cauldron is the essence of substance and pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Cauldron is the quintessence of substance and pattern.

sentences.zh: 知吉知凶，能重能輕，不炊而沸，五味自生，王者盛德則出。

translations.literal: It knows fortune and misfortune, can be heavy or light, boils without being heated, produces the five flavors of itself, and when a king possesses abundant virtue, it appears.
translations.idiomatic: It knows fortune and misfortune, can be heavy or light, boils without fire, produces the five flavors of itself, and when a ruler possesses abundant virtue, it appears.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝元鼎元年五月五日，得鼎汾水上。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanding of Emperor Wu of Han, on the fifth day of the fifth month, a cauldron was obtained on the Fen River.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanding under Emperor Wu of Han, on the fifth day of the fifth month, a cauldron was found on the banks of the Fen River.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝永平六年二月，廬江太守獻寶鼎。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Yongping of Emperor Ming of Han, the grand administrator of Lujiang presented a precious cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year of Yongping under Emperor Ming of Han, the grand administrator of Lujiang presented a precious cauldron.

sentences.zh: 出王雒山。

translations.literal: It came out of Mount Wangluo.
translations.idiomatic: It had emerged from Mount Wangluo.

sentences.zh: 雒或作雄。

translations.literal: Luo is also written as Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: For Luo, some texts read Xiong instead.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝建初七年十月，車駕西巡至槐里，右扶風禁上美陽得銅器於岐山，似酒尊。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year of Jianchu of Emperor Zhang of Han, the imperial carriage toured west to Huaili; an officer of the guard at Meiyang in Right Fufeng obtained a bronze vessel on Mount Qi, resembling a wine jar.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the seventh year of Jianchu under Emperor Zhang of Han, the emperor toured west as far as Huaili, where a guard officer of Meiyang in Right Fufeng obtained a bronze vessel on Mount Qi shaped like a wine jar.

sentences.zh: 詔在道晨夕以為百官熱酒。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that on the road, morning and evening, it be used to warm wine for the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that on the journey, morning and evening, it be used to warm wine for the court officials.

sentences.zh: 漢和帝永元元年，竇憲征匈奴，於漠北酒泉得仲山甫鼎，容五斗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan of Emperor He of Han, Dou Xian campaigned against the Xiongnu and at Jiuquan in the northern desert obtained the cauldron of Zhong Shanfu, with a capacity of five dou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan under Emperor He of Han, on Dou Xian's campaign against the Xiongnu, the cauldron of Zhong Shanfu was found at Jiuquan in the northern desert; it held five dou.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權赤烏十二年六月戊戌，寶鼎出臨平湖。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day of the sixth month of the twelfth year of Chiwu of Sun Quan of Wu, a precious cauldron emerged from Lake Linping.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the sixth month of the twelfth year of Chiwu under Sun Quan of Wu, a precious cauldron emerged from Lake Linping.

sentences.zh: 又出東部酃縣。

translations.literal: Another also emerged in Ling County in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Another also appeared in Ling County in the eastern region.

sentences.zh: 吳孫晧寶鼎元年八月，在所言得大鼎。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Baoding of Sun Hao of Wu, a great cauldron was obtained at his seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Baoding under Sun Hao of Wu, a great cauldron was found at his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和元年十月辛卯，宣城舂穀縣山岸崩，獲石鼎重二斤，受斛餘。

translations.literal: On the xinmao day of the tenth month of the first year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin, a mountain bank collapsed in Chungu County, Xuancheng, and a stone cauldron was obtained weighing two jin, with a capacity of slightly more than one hu.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the tenth month of the first year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng of Jin, a mountainside collapsed in Chungu County in Xuancheng, yielding a stone cauldron weighing two jin and holding slightly more than one hu.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康五年，豫章南昌民掘地得銅鍾四枚，太守褚裒以獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xiankang of Emperor Cheng of Jin, commoners of Nanchang in Yuzhang, digging earth, obtained four bronze bells; the grand administrator Chu Pou presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin, commoners of Nanchang in Yuzhang unearthed four bronze bells, and Grand Administrator Chu Pou presented them.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝升平五年二月乙未，南掖門有馬足陷地，得銅鍾一枚。

translations.literal: On the yiwei day of the second month of the fifth year of Shengping of Emperor Mu of Jin, at the South Side Gate a horse's hoof sank into the ground and one bronze bell was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day of the second month of the fifth year of Shengping under Emperor Mu of Jin, a horse's hoof sank into the ground at the South Side Gate, and one bronze bell was found.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十三年四月辛丑，武昌縣章山水側自開出神鼎，江州刺史南譙王義宣以獻。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day of the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, at the side of Mount Zhang in Wuchang County a divine cauldron opened of itself; Yixuan, Prince of Nanqiao and Inspector of Jiangzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, a divine cauldron opened of its own accord beside Mount Zhang in Wuchang County, and Yixuan, Prince of Nanqiao and Inspector of Jiangzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十九年九月戊申，廣陵肥如石梁澗中出石鍾九口，大小行次，引列南向，南兗州刺史臨川王義慶以獻。

translations.literal: On the wushen day of the ninth month of the nineteenth year of Yuanjia, nine stone bells emerged in the Stone Bridge Ravine at Feiru in Guangling, large and small in order, drawn up in a row facing south; Yiqing, Prince of Linchuan and Inspector of South Yanzhou, presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day of the ninth month of the nineteenth year of Yuanjia, nine stone bells appeared in the Stone Bridge Ravine at Feiru in Guangling, arranged by size in a row facing south, and Yiqing, Prince of Linchuan and Inspector of South Yanzhou, presented them.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十一年十二月，新陽獲古鼎於水側，有篆書四十二字，雍州刺史蕭思話以獻。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, Xinyang obtained an ancient cauldron beside the water, bearing forty-two characters in seal script; Xiao Sihua, Inspector of Yongzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, an ancient cauldron was found beside the water at Xinyang, inscribed with forty-two characters in seal script, and Xiao Sihua, Inspector of Yongzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年，豫章豫寧縣出銅鍾，江州刺史廣陵王紹以獻。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, a bronze bell emerged in Yunin County, Yuzhang; Shao, Prince of Guangling and Inspector of Jiangzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, a bronze bell appeared in Yunin County in Yuzhang, and Shao, Prince of Guangling and Inspector of Jiangzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝孝建三年四月丁亥，臨川宜黃縣民田中得銅鍾七口，內史傅徽以獻。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day of the fourth month of the third year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiao of Song, in the fields of Yihuang County in Linchuan seven bronze bells were obtained; the internal secretary Fu Hui presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the fourth month of the third year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiao of Song, seven bronze bells were found in the fields of Yihuang County in Linchuan, and Internal Secretary Fu Hui presented them.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年四月甲辰，晉陵延陵得古鍾六口，徐州刺史竟陵王誕以獻。

translations.literal: On the jiachen day of the fourth month of the third year of Xiaojian, six ancient bells were obtained at Yanling in Jinling; Dan, Prince of Jingling and Inspector of Xuzhou, presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the fourth month of the third year of Xiaojian, six ancient bells were found at Yanling in Jinling, and Dan, Prince of Jingling and Inspector of Xuzhou, presented them.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明七年六月，江夏蒲圻獲銅路鼓，四面獨足，郢州刺史安陸王子綏以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, a bronze road drum was obtained at Puqi in Jiangxia, with four faces and a single foot; Zisui, Prince of Anlu and Inspector of Yingzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, a bronze road drum with four faces and a single foot was found at Puqi in Jiangxia, and Zisui, Prince of Anlu and Inspector of Yingzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始四年二月丙申，豫章望蔡獲古銅鍾，高一尺七寸，圍二尺八寸，太守張辯以獻。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day of the second month of the fourth year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, an ancient bronze bell was obtained at Wangcai in Yuzhang, one chi seven cun high and two chi eight cun in circumference; the grand administrator Zhang Bian presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the second month of the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, an ancient bronze bell was found at Wangcai in Yuzhang, one chi seven cun high and two chi eight cun around, and Grand Administrator Zhang Bian presented it.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年五月壬戌，豫章南昌獲古銅鼎，容斛七斗，江州刺史王景文以獻。

translations.literal: On the renxu day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Taishi, an ancient bronze cauldron was obtained at Nanchang in Yuzhang, with a capacity of one hu and seven dou; Wang Jingwen, Inspector of Jiangzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Taishi, an ancient bronze cauldron holding one hu and seven dou was found at Nanchang in Yuzhang, and Wang Jingwen, Inspector of Jiangzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年六月甲寅，義陽郡獲銅鼎，受一斛，并蓋並隱起鏤，豫州刺史段佛榮以獻。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day of the sixth month of the seventh year of Taishi, a bronze cauldron was obtained in Yiyang Commandery, holding one hu, with its lid included; both cauldron and lid bore raised relief carving; Duan Furong, Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the sixth month of the seventh year of Taishi, a bronze cauldron holding one hu was found in Yiyang Commandery, lid included, both pieces carved in raised relief, and Duan Furong, Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 從帝昇明二年九月，建寧萬歲山澗中得銅鍾，長二尺一寸，豫州刺史劉懷珍以獻。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Shengming of the Deposed Emperor, a bronze bell was obtained in a ravine of Mount Wansui in Jianning, two chi one cun long; Liu Huaizhen, Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Shengming under the Deposed Emperor, a bronze bell two chi one cun long was found in a ravine on Mount Wansui in Jianning, and Liu Huaizhen, Inspector of Yuzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝元康二年夏，神雀集雍。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Yuankang of Emperor Xuan of Han, divine sparrows gathered at Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Yuankang under Emperor Xuan of Han, divine sparrows gathered at Yong.

sentences.zh: 元康三年春，神雀集泰山。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Yuankang, divine sparrows gathered at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Yuankang, divine sparrows gathered at Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 宣帝元康三年春，五色雀以萬數，飛過屬縣。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Yuankang of Emperor Xuan, multicolored sparrows in their tens of thousands flew over the subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Yuankang under Emperor Xuan, multicolored sparrows numbering in the tens of thousands flew over the subordinate counties.

sentences.zh: 元康四年三月，神雀五采以萬數，飛過集長樂、未央、北宮、高寢、甘泉泰畤殿。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Yuankang, divine sparrows in five colors, numbering in the tens of thousands, flew over and gathered at Changle, Weiyang, the Northern Palace, the High Chambers, and the Taichi Hall at Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year of Yuankang, divine sparrows in five colors, numbering in the tens of thousands, flew over and settled at Changle, Weiyang, the Northern Palace, the High Chambers, and the Taichi Hall at Ganquan.

sentences.zh: 元康四年，神雀仍集。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuankang, divine sparrows again gathered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuankang, divine sparrows gathered again.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝五鳳三年正月，神雀集京師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Wufeng of Emperor Xuan of Han, divine sparrows gathered at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Wufeng under Emperor Xuan of Han, divine sparrows gathered at the capital.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝永平十七年春，神雀五色集京師。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year of Yongping of Emperor Ming of Han, divine sparrows in five colors gathered at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year of Yongping under Emperor Ming of Han, divine sparrows in five colors gathered at the capital.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和中，神雀見郡國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang of Han, divine sparrows appeared in the commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era under Emperor Zhang of Han, divine sparrows appeared in the commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十二年，白鵲見新野鄧縣，雍州刺史蕭思話以聞

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, a white magpie appeared in Deng County, Xinye; Xiao Sihua, Inspector of Yongzhou, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, a white magpie appeared in Deng County in Xinye, and Xiao Sihua, Inspector of Yongzhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年五月癸酉，白鵲見建康崇孝里，揚州刺史始興王濬以獻。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day of the fifth month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, a white magpie appeared in Chongxiao Lane, Jiankang; Jun, Prince of Shixing and Inspector of Yangzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the fifth month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, a white magpie appeared in Chongxiao Lane in Jiankang, and Jun, Prince of Shixing and Inspector of Yangzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明七年三月辛巳，白鵲見汝南安陽，太守申令孫以獻。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day of the third month of the seventh year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, a white magpie appeared in Anyang, Runan; the grand administrator Shen Lingsun presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the third month of the seventh year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, a white magpie appeared in Anyang in Runan, and Grand Administrator Shen Lingsun presented it.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永嘉元年五月，白鼠見東宮，皇太子獲以獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yongjia of Emperor Hui of Jin, a white rat appeared in the Eastern Palace; the crown prince captured it and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Yongjia under Emperor Hui of Jin, a white rat appeared in the Eastern Palace, and the crown prince captured it and presented it.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝泰始三年二月壬寅，白鼠見樂安，青州刺史沈文秀以獻。

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the second month of the third year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, a white rat appeared in Le'an; Shen Wenxiu, Inspector of Qingzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day of the second month of the third year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, a white rat appeared in Le'an, and Shen Wenxiu, Inspector of Qingzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 漢昭帝始元元年二月，黃鵠下建章宮太液池中。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Shiyuan of Emperor Zhao of Han, a yellow swan descended into the Taiye Pool in Jianzhang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Shiyuan under Emperor Zhao of Han, a yellow swan descended into the Taiye Pool at Jianzhang Palace.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和二年二月，車駕東巡，柴祭岱宗。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Yuanhe of Emperor Zhang of Han, the imperial carriage toured east and performed a firewood offering to the Lord of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Yuanhe under Emperor Zhang of Han, the emperor toured east and performed the firewood offering to Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，黃鵠三十從西南來，經祠壇上東北過。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, thirty yellow swans came from the southwest, passed over the sacrificial altar, and went on toward the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, thirty yellow swans came from the southwest, passed over the sacrificial altar, and flew on toward the northeast.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝太初三年二月五日，行幸東海，獲赤雁。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the second month of the third year of Taichu of Emperor Wu of Han, traveling in favor to the Eastern Sea, a red wild goose was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the second month of the third year of Taichu under Emperor Wu of Han, while visiting the Eastern Sea, a red wild goose was caught.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝初，鑊中生赤魚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reign of Emperor Wen of Wei, red fish were born in a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the reign of Emperor Wen of Wei, red fish appeared in a cooking cauldron.

sentences.zh: 孫權時，神雀巢朱雀門。

translations.literal: In the time of Sun Quan, a divine sparrow nested at the Vermilion Bird Gate.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Sun Quan, a divine sparrow nested at the Vermilion Bird Gate.

sentences.zh: 孫晧天璽元年，臨海郡吏伍曜在海水際得石樹，高三尺餘，枝莖紫色，詰屈傾靡，有光采。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi of Sun Hao, the clerk Wu Yao of Linhai Commandery obtained a stone tree at the seashore, more than three chi high, with purple stems and branches, twisted and leaning, possessing luster.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi under Sun Hao, Wu Yao, a clerk of Linhai Commandery, found a stone tree at the seashore more than three chi high, its stems and branches purple, gnarled and leaning, bright with luster.

sentences.zh: 山海經所載玉碧樹之類也。

translations.literal: It is of the kind of jade and green-jade trees recorded in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.
translations.idiomatic: It was of the kind of jade and green-jade trees described in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始二年六月壬申，白鴿見酒泉延壽，延壽長王音以獻。

translations.literal: On the renshen day of the sixth month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, a white dove appeared at Yanshou in Jiuquan; Wang Yin, chief of Yanshou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day of the sixth month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, a white dove appeared at Yanshou in Jiuquan, and Wang Yin, chief of Yanshou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和九年五月癸酉，白鵝見吳國錢塘，內史虞潭以獻。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day of the fifth month of the ninth year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin, a white goose appeared at Qiantang in the state of Wu; Yu Tan, the internal secretary, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the fifth month of the ninth year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng of Jin, a white goose appeared at Qiantang in Wu, and Internal Secretary Yu Tan presented it.

sentences.zh: 安帝義熙元年，南康雩都嵩山有金雞，青黃色，飛集巖間。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin, on Mount Song of Yudu in Nankang there was a golden chicken, blue-yellow in color, flying and gathering among the cliffs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, a golden chicken, blue-yellow in color, flew and gathered among the cliffs on Mount Song at Yudu in Nankang.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十二年，湘州刺史南平王鑠獻赤鸚鵡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, Shuo, Prince of Nanping and Inspector of Xiangzhou, presented a red parrot.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, Shuo, Prince of Nanping and Inspector of Xiangzhou, presented a red parrot.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明三年正月丙申，媻皇國獻赤白鸚鵡各一。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day of the first month of the third year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, the kingdom of Panhuang presented one red and one white parrot.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the first month of the third year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, the kingdom of Panhuang presented one red parrot and one white parrot.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十四年十月甲午，揚州刺史始興王濬獻白鸚鵡。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day of the tenth month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, Jun, Prince of Shixing and Inspector of Yangzhou, presented a white parrot.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the tenth month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, Jun, Prince of Shixing and Inspector of Yangzhou, presented a white parrot.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明五年正月丙子，交州刺史垣閎獻白孔雀。

translations.literal: On the bingzi day of the first month of the fifth year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, Yuan Hong, Inspector of Jiaozhou, presented a white peacock.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day of the first month of the fifth year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, Yuan Hong, Inspector of Jiaozhou, presented a white peacock.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始三年五月乙亥，白鴝鵒見京兆，雍州刺史巴陵王休若以獻。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the fifth month of the third year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, a white myna appeared in Jingzhao; Xiuruo, Prince of Baling and Inspector of Yongzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the fifth month of the third year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, a white myna appeared in Jingzhao, and Xiuruo, Prince of Baling and Inspector of Yongzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝延熹九年四月，濟陰、東郡、濟北、平原河水清。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Yanxi of Emperor Huan of Han, the river waters of Jiyin, Dong, Jibei, and Pingyuan became clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Yanxi under Emperor Huan of Han, the river waters of Jiyin, Dong, Jibei, and Pingyuan ran clear.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉二十四年二月戊戌，河、濟俱清，龍驤將軍、青冀二州刺史杜坦以聞。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day of the second month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, the Yellow River and the Ji River both became clear; Du Tan, General of the Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the second month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, the Yellow River and the Ji River both ran clear, and Du Tan, General of the Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, reported it.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉二十五年五月，征北長史、廣陵太守范邈上言：「所領輿縣，前有大浦，控引潮流，水常淤濁。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen, Fan Miao, Chief Clerk of the Northern Campaign and grand administrator of Guangling, submitted a memorial: "In the counties under my jurisdiction there was formerly a great inlet that drew in the tidal flow, and the water was always muddy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, Fan Miao, Chief Clerk of the Northern Campaign and grand administrator of Guangling, submitted a memorial: "In the counties under my jurisdiction there was once a great inlet that drew in the tidal flow, and the water was always turbid.

sentences.zh: 自比以來，源流清潔，纖鱗呈形。

translations.literal: Since then the source and flow have been clear and pure, and the smallest fish show their forms.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the source and flow have become clear and pure, and even the smallest fish can be seen.

sentences.zh: 古老相傳，以為休瑞。」

translations.literal: The ancients handed down the tradition that this is a propitious sign."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients handed down the tradition that this is an auspicious sign."

sentences.zh: 孝武帝孝建三年九月，濟、河清，冀州刺史垣護之以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiao of Song, the Ji and the Yellow River became clear; Yuan Huzhi, Inspector of Jizhou, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiao of Song, the Ji and the Yellow River ran clear, and Yuan Huzhi, Inspector of Jizhou, reported it.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明五年九月庚戌，河、濟俱清，平原太守申纂以聞。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day of the ninth month of the fifth year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, the Yellow River and the Ji River both became clear; Shen Zuan, grand administrator of Pingyuan, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the ninth month of the fifth year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, the Yellow River and the Ji River both ran clear, and Shen Zuan, grand administrator of Pingyuan, reported it.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始元年二月丙寅，揚、淮水清潔有異於常，州治中從事史張緒以聞。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day of the second month of the first year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, the waters of the Yangtze and the Huai were clear and pure, unusual compared with the norm; Zhang Xu, Registrar of the provincial headquarters, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the second month of the first year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, the Yangtze and Huai ran unusually clear and pure, and Zhang Xu, Registrar of the provincial headquarters, reported it.

sentences.zh: 漢光武建武初，野繭、穀充給百姓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era of Emperor Guangwu of Han, wild cocoons and grain sufficed to supply the common people.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianwu era under Emperor Guangwu of Han, wild cocoons and grain sufficed to supply the common people.

sentences.zh: 其後耕蠶稍廣，二事漸息。

translations.literal: Afterward plowing and sericulture gradually spread, and the two phenomena gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, as farming and sericulture gradually expanded, both phenomena faded away.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權黃龍三年夏，野蠶繭大如卵。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year of Huanglong of Sun Quan of Wu, wild silkworm cocoons were as large as eggs.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year of Huanglong under Sun Quan of Wu, wild silkworm cocoons grew as large as eggs.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十六年，宣城宛陵廣野蠶成繭，大如雉卵，彌漫林谷，年年轉盛。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, in the broad wilds of Wanling, Xuancheng, wild silkworms formed cocoons as large as pheasant eggs, filling the forests and valleys, growing more abundant year by year.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, in the broad wilds of Wanling in Xuancheng, wild silkworms formed cocoons as large as pheasant eggs, spreading through the forests and valleys and growing more abundant year after year.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明三年五月癸巳，宣城宛陵縣石亭山生野蠶，三百餘里，太守張辯以聞。

translations.literal: On the guisi day of the fifth month of the third year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, wild silkworms appeared on Mount Shiting in Wanling County, Xuancheng, over more than three hundred li; the grand administrator Zhang Bian reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day of the fifth month of the third year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, wild silkworms appeared on Mount Shiting in Wanling County in Xuancheng over more than three hundred li, and Grand Administrator Zhang Bian reported it.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明三年十一月己巳，肅慎氏獻楛矢石砮，高麗國譯而至。

translations.literal: On the jisi day of the eleventh month of the third year of Daming of Emperor Xiao of Song, the Sushen people presented horn arrows and stone bola; they arrived through interpreters from the kingdom of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the eleventh month of the third year of Daming under Emperor Xiao of Song, the Sushen people presented horn arrows and stone bola, conveyed through interpreters from Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 大明五年正月戊午元日，花雪降殿庭。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day, New Year's Day of the first month of the fifth year of Daming, flower snow fell in the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, the wuwu day of the first month of the fifth year of Daming, flower snow fell in the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 時右衞將軍謝莊下殿，雪集衣。

translations.literal: At the time the General of the Right Guard, Xie Zhuang, was descending from the hall, and the snow gathered on his robes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, as General of the Right Guard Xie Zhuang was leaving the hall, the snow settled on his robes.

sentences.zh: 還白，上以為瑞。

translations.literal: Returning, he reported it, and the emperor regarded it as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported it, the emperor took it as an auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 於是公卿並作花雪詩。

translations.literal: Thereupon the high ministers all composed poems on the flower snow.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the high ministers all composed poems on the flower snow.

sentences.zh: 史臣按詩云：「先集為霰。

translations.literal: The historiographer notes that the Classic of Poetry says: "First it gathers as graupel.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer notes that the Classic of Poetry says, "First it gathers as graupel.

sentences.zh: 」韓詩曰：「霰，英也。

translations.literal: " The Han Poetry says: "Graupel is ying.
translations.idiomatic: " The Han Poetry says, "Graupel is ying.

sentences.zh: 」花葉謂之英。

translations.literal: " Flower petals are called ying.
translations.idiomatic: " Flower petals are called ying.

sentences.zh: 離騷云：「秋菊之落英。

translations.literal: Encountering Sorrow says: "The falling petals of autumn chrysanthemums.
translations.idiomatic: Encountering Sorrow says, "The falling petals of autumn chrysanthemums.

sentences.zh: 」左思云「落英飄颻」是也。

translations.literal: " Zuo Si's line "falling petals flutter" confirms this.
translations.idiomatic: " Zuo Si's line, "falling petals flutter," confirms this.

sentences.zh: 然則霰為花雪矣。

translations.literal: Thus graupel is flower snow.
translations.idiomatic: Thus graupel is flower snow.

sentences.zh: 草木花多五出，花雪獨六出。

translations.literal: The flowers of grasses and trees mostly have five points; flower snow alone has six.
translations.idiomatic: The flowers of grasses and trees are mostly five-pointed; flower snow alone is six-pointed.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始二年五月甲寅，赭中獲石栢長三尺二寸，廣三尺五寸，揚州刺史建安王休仁以獻。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day of the fifth month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song, a stone cypress was obtained at Zhè, two chi two cun long and three chi five cun wide; Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an and Inspector of Yangzhou, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the fifth month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, a stone cypress two chi two cun long and three chi five cun wide was found at Zhè, and Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an and Inspector of Yangzhou, presented it.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年十一月乙卯，盱眙獲石栢，寧朔將軍段佛榮以獻。

translations.literal: On the yimao day of the eleventh month of the third year of Taishi, a stone cypress was obtained at Xuyi; Duan Furong, General Who Pacifies the North, presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day of the eleventh month of the third year of Taishi, a stone cypress was found at Xuyi, and Duan Furong, General Who Pacifies the North, presented it.

sentences.zh: 漢和帝在位十七年，郡國言瑞應八十餘品，帝讓而不宣。

translations.literal: During the seventeen years of Emperor He's reign, the commanderies and kingdoms reported more than eighty kinds of auspicious responses; the emperor declined them and did not proclaim them.
translations.idiomatic: During the seventeen years of Emperor He's reign, the commanderies and kingdoms reported more than eighty kinds of auspicious signs, but the emperor modestly declined to proclaim them.
